item2: The photograph shows a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum. It originates from the Gernsheim Corpus and bears the number  gern_074197_post. The photograph was taken in black and white on April 22, 2004, and is part of the Donazione Gernsheim. It is a gift from Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and is currently restricted.

The drawing "Study of a Standing and a Reclining Nude before a River Landscape" is by Domenico Beccafumi and is in the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The first previous owner was Nicolas Lanière, the second previous owner was William (Duke, 2) Devonshire. The work was executed on white paper with red chalk and measures 224 x 158 mm.

The drawing is part of the Devonshire Collection and has been mentioned in the literature, for example, in "The Devonshire Collection..." by M. Jaffé, published in 1994.

The curator of the Chatsworth House private collection is the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The second previous owner of the collection was the Devonshire private collection, William (Duke, 2). The first previous owner is unknown and the collection was in the private collection of Nicolas Lanière.

The image depicts a standing figure with their arm outstretched upwards and looking upwards. The figure is lying on its side with the upper part of the body raised and leaning on their arm. The background shows a valley.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Corpus. The image is numbered bh_gern_073540_post and was donated on October 1, 2011 by the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta.

The curator of the Copenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst, Kupferstichkabinett, possesses an Italian drawing signed "Tu ital.mag.XV.55". The sheet depicts a boar killing Adonis and is titled "A Boar Kills Adonis". It is an oval drawing on light brown paper executed in pen and ink. The dimensions are 58 x 76 mm.

The drawing is listed as number 92 C 49 15 in the Gernsheim catalogue and is listed there under "Meleager and the Boar". It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett. The object itself bears the inventory number XV.55 and is located in the Italian magazine.
The picture depicts the death of Adonis. He is killed by a boar.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection within the Gernsheim Collection. The image is catalogued as "Corpus Gernsheim g-art" and was donated to the museum on July 25, 2003, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The work is currently closed to the public.

The curator of the Uffizi Gallery, Florence, published drawing 6549 in the collection "Disegni e Stampe". It was previously attributed to Rosa, but this attribution was rejected by Mahoney. The work depicts two antique draped figures and is an example of 17th-century drawing. It is a pen and ink drawing on paper, executed with a brush and wash. The dimensions are 80 x 71 mm. 

Mahoney, in his work "The Drawings of Salvator Rosa", mentions the drawing on page 778. The drawing is also found in the catalog of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The custodian is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi with the object number 6549 S.
The picture shows a man from history being crowned with a laurel wreath while talking to someone else.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings is shown here. It comes from the Gernsheim Corpus and bears the number bh_gern_053066_post. The photograph was donated on June 12, 2006, by the Gernsheim Collection, Walter and Jutta. The photograph belongs to the category "g-art".

Published by the Curator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage, Berlin State Museums - Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints, the drawing 295-1844 KdZ is in the collection. The drawing is attributed to Federico Barocci. It is a study for his painting "The Descent from the Cross" in the Cathedral of Perugia. The drawing shows leg, knee, and drapery studies of Christ for the painting. A wide strip has been torn from the left edge. The drawing is firmly mounted on a collector's passe-partout.

The drawing is white chalk on black chalk and is on blue paper measuring 417 x 282 mm. It bears the inventory number 31 A 22 5 31 A 22 52 41 D 27. A publication by A. Emiliani, Federico Barocci, Bologna 1985, lists the drawing under Kat. 131. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns another copy of the drawing.

The curator of the collection of drawings and prints 295-1844 KdZ is the Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Museums Berlin. The administration of this object is handled by the Berlin Administrator.
The image depicts the legs of a person with a bent knee, wearing an outfit adorned with pleats.

The photograph depicts the work "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings" from the Gernsheim Collection. It was donated to the museum by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta Gernsheim) on May 1, 2007. The photograph is signed "gern_060816_post" and is part of the "g-art" collection.

The drawing "Classical Landscape with Ruin" is by Johannes de Bosch and was made in 1713. It was published by the administrator of the Kunsthalle Bremen. The work is a pen and ink drawing, washed with watercolor, and executed in black and gray. The drawing measures 210 x 288 mm. It is part of the Gernsheim catalogue, mentioned on page 1299. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns the drawing.
The Bremen Kunsthalle is managed by the administrator in Bremen.
The image depicts an idyllic landscape with ruins.
A photograph from the Albertina dating from 1990 is restricted.

The drawing "Sketches of an Ancient Horse's Head" was published by Raffael Santi, Raffaello Umkreis, Raffaello Sanzio, or Raffaele Raffaello Santi Raphael Urbinas Raphaello Raffael. It originates from the Graphic Collection Albertina in Vienna and was produced by the Vienna Administrator. The drawing is executed on brown paper with pen and wash technique. It measures 197 x 255 mm and has the inventory number 48 C 2 : 46 C 13 14 1.  

The drawing is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Graphic Collection Albertina in Vienna is the Albertina.
The image shows a sculpture of a seated man holding a letter.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings is held in the Gernsheim Corpus. The photograph is designated bh_gern_071270_post and was acquired on March 9, 2005, as a gift from the Gernsheims, Walter and Jutta, and added to the Corpus. The photograph is catalogued under g-art.

The drawing "Stage Design Sketch" by Felice Donghi was published by the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice. The pen and ink drawing measures 210 x 249 mm and is part of the Gernsheim catalogue. It is held in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administration of the property is handled by the Fondazione Giorgio Cini in Venice.
The image depicts a stage backdrop.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim Corpus. The image is numbered bh_gern_073541_post and was donated on October 1, 2011 by the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph is available for use.

The copper engraving by Antonio Vassilacchi from 1550/1599 depicts a scene from Venetian history. The wash drawing, measuring 200 x 265 mm, is in the possession of the Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett in Copenhagen and can be found there under the number GB 8487. The attribution of the work to Vicentino was suggested by Terisio Pignatti. The work was presented in the publication "Venetian Drawings" by C. Fischer, 2018, Copenhagen.

The drawing is part of the Gernsheim Katalogliste anonimo and is kept at the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom.
The custodian of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett with the signature GB 8487. The object itself is listed in the catalog under the number Tu ital.mag.XV.56.
The image depicts historical events and situations in Venice.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and comes from the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The image is numbered and was donated to the museum in 2007 by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph was taken in 1831 and is classified as "g-art".

A sketchbook by Pietro Novelli from 1565, inv. 1565/31, is located in the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo, more precisely in the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia. The sketchbook was made by Novelli, Pietro and drawn by Monrealese, il Pietro Novelli. The motif depicts John the Baptist. The drawing is executed on ivory-colored paper with black ink and measures 260 x 228 mm. 

The drawing is mentioned in the publication "Pietro Novelli e il suo ambiente, Palermo 1990" on page 400, catalogue number III.30a. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The caretaker of the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo, Sicily, is the owner of a sketchbook that is held in the Regional Museum of Sicily under the inventory number 1565. The sketchbook dates from 1565 and is numbered 1565/31.
The picture shows John the Baptist.

The photograph depicts the "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings" from the collection of the "Corpus Gernsheim". The photograph dates from 1825 and is signed "bh_gern_182511_post". The image was donated to the museum on February 18, 2010, as part of the "Donazione Gernsheim" by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The sketchbook (inv. 5239) from the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia in Palermo was published by the curator. The drawing bears the number 5239/34 and dates from 1601/1700. It consists of figure studies in drawing, executed in chalk on red ground. The drawing measures 113 x 223 mm and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue under the number 49 D 11 (2) : 31 A 23 31 31 A 23 1.

The drawing is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was published anonymously.

The Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia administrator manages the sketchbook with inventory number 5239. 

The sketchbook is owned by the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia and bears the inventory number 5239/34.
The picture shows two standing figures.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is shown here. The image bears the identification number bh_gern_060815_post and was added to the collection on May 1, 2007. It comes from the Gernsheim Donation, donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and is presented as part of the "g-art" collection series.

The curator of the Kunsthalle Bremen has published the work "The Emmaus Meal" by Andries Both. The work is a drawing in chalk and pen, washed with ink. It measures 188 x 196 mm and is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. Andries Both was a Dutch artist active in the 17th century.
The administrator of the Kunsthalle Bremen is the Bremen Administration.
The image depicts the scene of the Last Supper in Emmaus, where Christ is recognized while blessing or breaking the bread.
A photograph from the Albertina dating from 1990 is restricted.

The drawing "Seated Madonna with Child" was made by Perin del Vaga, possibly in collaboration with Pietro Buonaccorsi or Pierino del Vaga. The sheet is executed on blue paper with chalk, ink, and pen in a wash technique. It measures 84 x 57 mm and was acquired for 11 FF 42 2. The drawing is in the Albertina's Graphic Collection in Vienna.

The "Seated Madonna with Child" is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana collection in Rome.
The administrator of the Vienna Graphic Collection Albertina is the institution Vienna. The Albertina is a significant collection of graphic art located in Vienna.
The picture shows Mary, seated or enthroned, with the Christ Child on her lap. The Christ Child is sitting on Mary's right knee.

The photograph shows a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. The drawing comes from the Corpus Gernsheim and has the number  _gern_149377_post. It was donated to the collection on February 14, 2005 by the Gernsheims, Walter and Jutta. The drawing is shown at the top.

The curator of the Kunstpalast Museum in Düsseldorf published a drawing by Giovanni Battista Gaulli, also known as il Bacciccia, in 1957. The drawing, which shows studies for a ceiling decoration, is a work of graphic art and was created with ink, chalk, and pen on paper. A pen was used as a tool. The ink is in gray, the chalk in black, and the ink in brown. The drawing measures 127 x 203 mm and bears the inventory number 31 A 23. 

The drawing was mentioned in the publication "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli" by D. Graf in 1976 and listed in the catalog under number 341. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns the drawing.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is the FP 1957.
The image depicts a seated sphinx, composed of the body of a lioness and the head of a woman. It is adorned with intricate ornaments.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection, is signed bh_gern_046615_post. It comes from the Gernsheim family collection, donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph was donated on July 11, 2006, and is marked g-art.

Curator of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints, published the drawing "Joshua's Victory". Nicolas Poussin, the draftsman, created the work around 1630. Originally, the drawing was attributed to Pietro Berrettini. The work is a chalk drawing on toned light brown paper. Details were applied with a pen in brown and chalk in red and black. The drawing measures 246 x 410 mm. 

The work is in the collection of the Berlin Print Room. The Print Room is part of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. It was presented in the catalogue of the exhibition "The Berlin Print Room: A Handbook to the Collection", edited by Alexander Dückers, in 1994 in Berlin.
The property manager is the institution "Administrator Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints KdZ".
The picture depicts Joshua and his army surprising the Amorites who are besieging the city of Gibeon.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and originates from the Gernsheim Collection. The image is signed bh_gern_028401_post and was donated on July 25, 2003, by the Gernsheim Donation, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph is currently restricted.

The former curator of the Uffizi, Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, possesses a drawing with the inventory number 6564 S. The drawing was formerly attributed to Salvator Rosa, but this attribution was rejected by Mahoney. The work depicts a back view of a seated man and is a pen and ink drawing on paper, executed with hatched tones. The dimensions are 85 x 61 mm. The drawing is part of the collection 31 A 23 5 31 D 1 (+2).

Mahoney, the author of the book "The drawings of Salvator Rosa" published in New York 1977, mentions the drawing on page 780. The drawing is also found in the catalog list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi with object number 6564 S.
The image depicts a seated figure representing the various stages of human life.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Corpus Gernsheim and bears the number  _gern_180539_post. It comes from the collection Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph was acquired in 2005 and is listed under the classification g-art.

The drawing "Peter is visited by an angel in prison" is attributed to Giovanni Bonatti (1635). It was published by the State Graphic Collection Munich. The drawing is attributed to the Italian artist Giovanni Bonatti, who was active in the 17th century. The drawing depicts Peter being visited by an angel in prison. The work is a red chalk drawing on chamois-colored paper.
The administrator of the State Graphic Collection in Munich is the Verwalter München.
The image depicts an angel opening the door of a prison at night. The scene portrays the escape of the Apostle Peter from prison.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings collection is held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The photograph, designated bh_gern_060818_post, was donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim to the Corpus on May 1, 2007. The image is classified as g-art and is currently restricted.

The coastal landscape with a sailing ship in stormy seas was drawn by Hendrik van der Borcht (the Younger). The drawing was created in 1614 and is executed in pen and wash. It measures 141 x 282 mm and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Kunsthalle Bremen, who published the drawing, is Hendrik van der Borcht (the Younger).
The administrator of the Bremen Kunsthalle is the Bremen Administration. The contact information is 59/284.
The picture shows a seascape on the coast.
A photo from the Albertina from 1990 is restricted.

The drawing "John and the Praying Madonna" is by the artist Giuseppe Agellio and was published by the Albertina Graphische Sammlung in Vienna. The work is a study in red chalk, pastel, and pen, executed in shades of gray and white. The drawing measures 213 x 210 mm and bears the signature "11 H (JOHN)". The inventory number is 73 A 35 2. The artist Agellio was part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Albertina's Graphic Collection in Vienna is responsible for inventory number 547.
The picture shows John the Baptist and Mary in a prayerful pose.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection, is shown here. The image is numbered bh_gern_074198_post and was donated on April 22, 2004, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The collection is held by the g-dis.

The artist who created the work depicting a kneeling draped figure is unknown. The work, a study in paper and metalpoint with white gouache, was created around 1401/1500 in Umbria. It measures 235 x 182 mm and bears the signature 31 A 23 31 (+2) 41 D 27.

Previously, the artwork was held in various private collections. It was first exhibited in 1698 in the collection of Marchetti, Matteo (Bishop) in Arezzo. Later, it passed into the collection of Summers,? (Lord) in London. In 1717, it finally came into the collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement in Chatsworth House, where it is currently located.

The curator of Chatsworth House is the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The first owner was the private collection of Resta, Sebastiano (Padre). It then passed into the private collection of Arezzo, where it was owned by Marchetti, Matteo (Bishop). The third owner was Summers,? (Lord) from London, who owned it from 1710 to 1716. It then came into the private collection of Chatsworth House, where it was acquired by Devonshire, William (Duke, 2).
The image depicts a person kneeling on both knees, dressed in a garment with folds.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. It comes from the Corpus Gernsheim collection and has the inventory number [removed]. The image was donated to the museum on October 1, 2011, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. Publication approval was granted by the Gernsheim family.

The curator of the Kupferstichkabinett at the Statens Museum for Kunst in Copenhagen has published the work "Martyrium verschiedener Heiliger". The work is a drawing by Francesco Solimena, or an artist of the Solimena school. The original is in the possession of the Gernsheim Collection. The drawing is executed in chalk and pen, washed in black and blue. It measures 406 x 270 mm and is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The custodian of the object is the Kopenhagen Statens Museum for Kunst Kupferstichkabinett. The object has the inventory number Tu ital.mag.XVI.53.
The image depicts a scene in which saints are carrying out a military attack.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and comes from the holdings of the Corpus Gernsheim. It bears the signature and was donated on February 18, 2010, by the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta.

The sketchbook (inv. 5239) of the Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia curator contains a drawing, probably of Sicilian origin. The drawing, created around 1701/1800, depicts the head of a man and was executed in chalk on light blue paper measuring 200 x 174 mm. The work is part of the Gernsheim catalogue and is listed as anonymous in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The administrator of Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia manages the sketchbook (inv. 5239/36) with the inventory number 5239/36.
The picture shows a human head.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of photographs of drawings. It was donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and belongs to the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The photograph was received on May 1, 2007.

The photograph is part of the "g-art" collection and has the number 2007.05.01.

The drawing "View of a Classical Portrait Relief" was created by Pieter Borm in 1704. The work is a red chalk drawing on paper measuring 327 x 260 mm. The drawing is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue under number 48 (+32 1) 61 B 11 1 (+51 3). The drawing was published by the Kunsthalle Bremen.
The administration of the Kunsthalle Bremen is the responsibility of the Bremen Kunsthalle Administrator, registered under number 53/290.
The image depicts an anonymous historical figure, shown alone.

This consideration focuses on a photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus. The photograph is designated bh_gern_020117_post and was donated to the Corpus on June 12, 2006, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

Published by the administrator of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints, the study is part of the collection 295-1844 KdZ. The drawing is attributed to Federico Barocci, also known as Federigo Fiori da Urbino, il Fiori, il Federico Barocci. The work is a study for the painting "Descent from the Cross" in the Cathedral of Perugia. It is a double rendering, showing two foot studies for the man on the ladder to the left in the painting. The bottom edge is slightly diagonally cut and there is a small gap in the middle of the top edge. The drawing is firmly mounted on a collector's passe-partout.

The study is a preparatory drawing executed in black and red chalk, white gouache, on blue paper. It measures 371 x 268 mm and is cataloged as 31 A 22 53 A. The work was mentioned by Emiliani, Federico in the publication "Federico Barocci, Bologna 1985" as Kat. 126. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information.

The curator of the collection of drawings and prints 295-1844 KdZ is the Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage.

The responsibility lies with the curator in Berlin.
The image shows a human leg extending to the lower leg.

As part of the Gernsheim donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim, which took place on July 1, 2006, the photograph "Corpus Gernsheim post" was added to the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. The photograph is classified as part of the g-art collection and bears the designation "post".

The drawing was published in 2000 by the administrator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The drawing KdZ 5176 dates from 1902 and was until then in a private Berlin collection. Previously, it was in London in the collections of William Russell and Benjamin West. 

The drawing "Jason before Pelias" was created in Pordenone by Giovanni Antonio de Lodesanis. It is a preliminary drawing for a fresco in Palazzo Doria Genua. The pen drawing on light brown paper is executed in brown and blue and measures 237 x 278 mm. It bears two stamps on the bottom left: Lugt I, 2648 and Lugt I, 419. The drawing can be viewed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome and the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, Kupferstichkabinett.

The administrator of the objects is the Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The collection includes works from the years 2000 to 1902 and bears the identifier KdZ 5176. The object was in a private collection in Berlin before 1902, owned by Adolf von Beckerath. 

Previously, it was in two private collections in London: the Russell Collection, William, and the West Collection, Benjamin.
The picture depicts the story of the Argonauts: their quest for the golden fleece.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and bears the signature bh_gern_183182_post. It is part of the Gernsheim Collection and was added to the museum in 2007 through a donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photographs were classified within the "g-art" collection.

A sketchbook by the artist Pietro Novelli, dated 1565, is located in the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo. The work, with the inventory number 1565, is part of the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia. The drawing, executed in brown and ink with a pen on ivory-colored paper, depicts the martyrdom of Saint Placidus and Saint Flavia.

The drawing was part of the exhibition "Pietro Novelli e il suo ambiente" in Palermo in 1990 and was presented on page 412 in the catalog under number III.54. The sketchbook is kept in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia Palazzo Abatellis is the owner of the sketchbook (inv. 1565), which was created in 1565. The sketchbook has the inventory number 1565/28.
The image depicts two female saints, possibly named Flavia and Placid.
A photograph from the Albertina dating from 1990 is restricted.

The drawing "Marriage of Mary" is from the collection of the Albertina Graphische Sammlung in Vienna. It was created by Antonio Viviani, also known as Antonio Antoniano da Urbino, around the year 1560. The drawing is in brown crayon and pen, washed in sepia, on brown paper. It measures 160 x 277 mm and is part of collection 73 A 42 of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The drawing was recorded there on December 1, 2014.
The administrator of the Graphic Collection Albertina in Vienna is the Albertina.
The picture shows the wedding of Mary and Joseph, who are being married by the High Priest.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings collection is held in the Gernsheim Corpus collection. The photograph is numbered  and was donated to the Corpus on April 21, 2004 by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta).

The drawing "Portrait Study of a Young Man" measuring 168 x 122 mm is part of the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement and was previously held by 13 previous owners. The work is by Francesco Salviati and was executed after a design by Cecchino Salviati and Francesco de' Rossi. The drawing is in red chalk on white paper. 

The work is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was described by M. Jaffé in the 1994 publication "The Devonshire Collection...".
The manager of Chatsworth House is the private collection Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The previous owner was the private collection Devonshire, William (Duke, 2).
The image depicts an anonymous historical figure, shown alone.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. It is catalogued under the number bh_gern_154737_post and was donated on January 10, 2006, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is classified as "g-art".

The drawing "Coronation of Saint Agatha" is listed in the catalog of the Biblioteca Reale in Turin as a work by Sodoma. It was previously attributed to the draftsman Bertini. In 1958, it was listed in Gernsheim's catalog (Cat. 411). The catalog lists the drawing as Lombard and dates it between 1601 and 1615. 

The drawing is a chalk drawing on paper and has been squared. It measures 293 x 218 mm. The signature "AGATHA" is 11 HH in size, while the signature "G" is 11 G in size and the signature "G.C." is 23 G in size. The drawing was listed in Sciolla's catalog "From Leonardo to Rembrandt" (Turin 1989) with catalog number 78.
The administrator of the Turin Royal Library is Turin.
The image depicts a holy Agatha, crowned by angels and honored with palm branches.

The photograph depicts a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. It originates from the Gernsheim Corpus and bears the number  gern_060820_post. The drawing was donated to the art museum on May 1, 2007, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

The allegorical depiction of August is a work by the draftsman Hans Bol, who is also credited with its creation. The drawing was made with pen and watercolor and is blue watercolor. The sheet measures 122 x 125 mm and bears the inventory number 23 N 32. 

The drawing is in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and, according to the Gernsheim catalogue list, page 1299, can be found there. The Kunsthalle Bremen manages the work.
The administrator of the Kunsthalle Bremen is the Kunsthalle Bremen. The administration is based in Bremen.
The image depicts August connected to other concepts.
In 1989, a photograph from the Albertina was restricted.

The drawing "Allegory of Servitude, the Young Captive" by Andrea Mantegna's circle is from the Albertina Graphic Collection in Vienna. The work, executed in red chalk and pen, depicts a young captive and measures 189 x 130 mm. The signature reads 44 G 31 2 46 A 12 51. The drawing is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Graphic Collection Albertina in Vienna is the Albertina.
The image depicts a prisoner in shackles, serving as a page or footman.

The photograph shows the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a work from the collection of the Corpus Gernsheim. The photograph was taken on November 7, 2003, and is part of the Donazione Gernsheim, donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "The Holy Family with the John the Baptist" is by Giovanni Battista Paggi and was made in 1554. The paper sheet was drawn with ink and worked with a pen in brown and sepia. The dimensions are 208 x 242 mm. The drawing was acquired by the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection, in 1872. Previously, it was in a private collection in Genoa, which belonged to the Durazzo family until 1872. 

"The Holy Family with the John the Baptist" is part of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart collection and was already mentioned in the publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem from 1977, catalogue number 39. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has documentation on this work.

The curator of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection 6328, is the 1872 purchase. Prior to that, the object was in a private collection in Genoa before it came into the possession of Durazzo, Jacopo, in 1872.
The picture depicts the Holy Family with John the Baptist as a child.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and originates from the Gernsheim Collection. The image is identified as bh_gern_020118_post and was donated on June 12, 2006 by the Gernsheim Donation, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta.

This drawing was published by the curator of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. Robert de Cotte, an 18th-century draftsman, left behind a series of drawings that meticulously capture the architecture of Venice. The drawings, located in the Bibliothèque Nationale in Paris and the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, depict landmarks such as St. Mark's Square, St. Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace, and the Biblioteca Marciana. Cotte used various techniques, including ink, pen, brush, and pencil, to create these masterpieces. His drawings offer a fascinating glimpse into Venetian architecture of the 18th century.

His works can be found in various publications, such as Jestaz's "Le voyage d'Italie" (1966). Cotte drew, among other things, a floor plan with St. Mark's Square, St. Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace, and the library, a floor plan of the Doge's Palace with the Doge's apartments, and an elevation of the Biblioteca Marciana and Procurazie Nuove.

The drawings are from the collection of the manager of the Paris Bibliothèque Nationale, Cabinet d'Estampes, and are located in the album "Drawing Art Architectural Drawing" at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. They were made by Robert de Cotte and depict floor plans and views of various buildings in Venice, including St. Mark's Square with St. Mark's Church, the Doge's Palace, and the Library. The drawings were executed in ink, pen, and brush on paper and are part of the Jestaz collection, which was published in 1966 in the work "Le voyage d'Italie".

Another work by Robert de Cotte, also from the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, depicts a floor plan of the Doge's Palace with the Doge's apartments. The drawing was created in pencil and ink on paper. Another drawing by Cotte shows a section through the Biblioteca Marciana and the Procurazie Nuove, with a cut through the arcades. On the back of the drawing is a floor plan of the southeast corner. All the drawings are detailed with annotations and measurements and were also published in Jestaz's work "Le voyage d'Italie".

The work "Grotesque Head of an Older Man in Academic Dress" was drawn by Leonardo da Vinci. The drawing on paper was done in brown ink and pen. It is 67 x 54 mm in size and bears the inventory number 32 A 5 : 31 A 22 1 (+3) 49 B 43 (+31). The work was acquired by the J. Paul Getty Museum in Malibu in 1984. The purchase was made through an auctioneer in London, Christie's, on July 3, 1984. 

Prior to its purchase by the J. Paul Getty Museum, the work was in a private collection. The fourth previous owner was Chatsworth House, which owned it in a private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement from 1982 to 1984. The third previous owner was also Chatsworth House, in the private collection of William (Duke, 2) Devonshire. The second previous owner was the private collection of Nicolaes Anthoni Flinck. The first previous owner was the private collection of Thomas (Arundel, Earl) Howard. The work is documented in the literature, including M. Jaffé, The Devonshire Collection..., London 1994, Kat. 883 and the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the J. Paul Getty Museum in Malibu acquired the object on July 3, 1984. Christie's auction house in London was the auctioneer on that day. The object had previously been in private ownership four times. It first belonged to the private collection of Thomas Howard, the Earl of Arundel. Subsequently, it passed into the collection of Nicolaes Anthoni Flinck.  Then it came into the possession of the Devonshire family, more precisely the private collection of William (Duke, 2) Devonshire. 

Finally, the object was in the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement, which were associated with Chatsworth House, until 1984.

The work was created with charcoal, white lead, and red chalk and is on a fully preserved collector's passe-partout. 

Further information about the drawing can be found in the publication by A. Emiliani "Federico Barocci, Bologna 1985". There the drawing is listed under number Kat. 717.

The drawing shows head studies and was executed in chalk on grayish-green paper. 

The drawing is 138 x 301 mm in size and bears the signature "ghiht" in red on white paper. It is documented in the work "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" by the Kunstmuseum Düsseldorf by Graf, Dieter. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome possesses another copy of the drawing.

The attribution to Elsheimer is mentioned in the literature, such as in the publication "The Drawings of Adam Elsheimer" by J. Jacoby (2008). The work is also in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.

Measuring 360 x 261 mm, it is part of the Italian drawings of the Berlin Art Library and was already cataloged in 1975 in the publication "Italian Drawings of the Berlin Art Library" by S. Jacob.  

The drawing is kept in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the collection is the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin - Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Kunstbibliothek. The object number within the collection is HdZ 3823.

The drawing "Virgin with Holy Alo" is located in the Royal Library of Windsor Castle and bears the inventory number RL 5248. It was produced by Giacomo Cavedone and is to be understood as a design for the painting "Virgin with Holy Alo" in the Pinacoteca Bologna. The drawing is a charcoal drawing on oil paper and measures 349 x 220 mm. 

Cavedone is also listed as a draftsman for the "British Museum List". The drawing is part of the Queen's collection and was catalogued in Kurz' work "Bolognese drawings of the XVII XVIII centuries in the Collection of her Majesty the Queen at Windsor Castle" published in 1988.

The curator of the Windsor Castle Royal Library is Windsor.

The design for the Church of San Pietro in the Vatican in Rome is by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger and was made between 1534 and 1537. The drawing is in ink, chalk, and pen on paper and shows a floor plan of the church. The colors of the drawing are brown and light brown (ink), red (chalk), and light yellow and gray (pen). 

The design was published in 1900 by Ch. Frommel and N. Adams in the publication "The architectural drawings of Antonio da Sangallo the Younger and his circle, vol. II" in Cambridge. The drawing is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Florence Collection, Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi, is responsible for object U 39 A recto.

The Codex Coner, a sketchbook from the workshop of Bernardo della Volpaia, was created between 1512 and 1515. The 232 x 167 mm work is located in Sir John Soane's Museum in London and can be found under the museum number Vol 115. It contains drawings of ancient architecture in Rome, including a composite capital, column bases, cornice details, voussoirs and impost stones of the Septimius and Titus arches, and animal ornaments.

The drawings were documented by Thomas Ashby in his work "Sixteenth-Century Drawings of Roman Buildings" (London 1904) and are archived in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under various catalogue numbers. These include drawings that refer to buildings such as the Mausoleum of Romulus, the Temple of Minerva, the Santi Quattro Coronati, and the San Paolo fuori le Mura.

The curator of Sir John Soane's Museum in London manages the "Codex Coner" collection (museum number "Vol 115"). The collection is accessible online and can be filtered by title and museum number using an advanced search. The search can also be sorted by "Order".

The drawing "The Holy Annunciation" by Annibale Carracci is from the collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement and was previously in private ownership. From 1710 to 1716 it was in the collection of William, the second Duke of Devonshire, in London.  

Later, the drawing came into the possession of four other previous owners before finally entering the collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The drawing "The Holy Annunciation" was executed by Annibale Carracci on brown paper with ink and pen and has the dimensions 160 x 141 mm.

The Codex Mellon, also known as the "Menicantonio Sketchbook," is an architectural sketchbook created by the Italian artist Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli around 1513. The 52-page codex, now in the Pierpont Morgan Library, contains numerous architectural drawings, sketches, and studies. The sketchbook primarily focuses on Roman architecture, featuring detailed representations of ancient monuments like the Pantheon, the Colosseum, Trajan's Column, and the Temple of Vesta. Chiarelli meticulously documented details of these structures, including their facades, interiors, and decorative elements.  

Beyond Roman architecture, the Codex Mellon also shows Chiarelli's interest in Renaissance architecture, with sketches of designs by architects like Bramante, Sangallo, and Peruzzi. The sketchbook offers a valuable insight into the artistic and architectural landscape of 16th-century Italy, highlighting Chiarelli's keen eye for detail and his profound understanding of both classical and contemporary architectural styles.

The Codex Mellon is held by the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York, more specifically in the Department of Drawings and Prints. The shelfmark is PML 1978.44 B3 027 08. Previously, the Codex was in a private collection in Washington, owned by Paul Mellon. 

It then moved to a private collection in New York owned by Hans Peter Kraus. Before its time in New York, the Codex was in a private collection in Bologna owned by Aimo Domenico and subsequently in a private collection in Rome owned by Carlo Fontana.

The Codex Mellon, a sketchbook by the Italian architect Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli, is a treasure trove of architectural drawings dating back to 1513. The codex, held at the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York, features sketches and designs of ancient Roman architecture, including temples, basilicas, and tombs. Chiarelli meticulously documented details like capitals, friezes, and decorative elements, demonstrating his keen eye for architectural intricacies. 

The sketchbook also reveals Chiarelli's fascination with the works of renowned architects like Raphael and Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, whose designs he studied and adapted in his own work. The Codex Mellon offers a valuable glimpse into the artistic and intellectual landscape of Renaissance Rome, showcasing the enduring influence of classical architecture on subsequent generations of architects.

The Codex Mellon (Sketchbook of Menicantonio) is an architectural sketchbook dating back to 1513. Created by Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli, it contains numerous drawings of architectural details, including Doric and Ionic capitals, temple facades, and elements of Roman buildings. The sketchbook also features sketches of fountains, sculptures, and other decorative motifs.  It offers a glimpse into the artistic and architectural practices of the early Renaissance, particularly in Rome, where Chiarelli studied and worked. 

The Codex Mellon is divided into 80 folios and showcases Chiarelli's meticulous observation and technical skill. Among the prominent subjects depicted are the Mausoleum of the Plautii in Tivoli, the Temple of Trajan, the Pantheon, and the Basilica Aemilia. The sketchbook also includes sketches of churches and other religious structures, as well as designs for palaces and public buildings.  The drawings are primarily executed in pen and ink, with some wash and brown ink techniques employed for added depth and shading. The Codex Mellon provides invaluable insights into the architectural heritage of Rome during the Renaissance and the artistic legacy of Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli.

The Codex Mellon is held by the New York Pierpont Morgan Library, Department of Drawings and Prints, under the accession number PML 1978.44 B3 027 08. It was previously in various private collections. It was first in the collection of Paul Mellon in Washington, then in the collection of Hans Peter Kraus in New York.

It was also in the collection of Aimo Domenico in Bologna and finally in the collection of Carlo Fontana in Rome.

The Codex Mellon (Sketchbook of Menicantonio) is a sketchbook by Antonio di Domenico Chiarelli, attributed to Domenico Chiarelli, dating from 1513. The sketchbook, measuring 21.3 x 14.6 cm, consists of 80 folios and contains numerous architectural drawings, primarily of Roman buildings. The drawings range from detailed studies of specific elements, such as capitals and cornices, to full-scale reconstructions of entire structures, including the Pantheon, the Colosseum, and Trajan's Forum.

The Codex Mellon is a valuable resource for understanding the architectural practices of the High Renaissance. Chiarelli's meticulous observations and skillful rendering capture the grandeur and complexity of Roman architecture. His sketches often include annotations and measurements, demonstrating his deep understanding of classical design principles. The sketchbook also provides insights into the development of architectural theory and the influence of classical antiquity on Renaissance art.

The Codex Mellon is held by the Pierpont Morgan Library in New York. The Library's Drawings and Prints Department houses the object under the accession number PML 1978.44 B3 027 08. It was previously in a private collection in Washington, owned by Paul Mellon.

Before it came to Washington, the Codex was in a private collection in New York owned by Hans Peter Kraus. The Codex's earlier history is less well known. It is believed to have been kept in private collections in Bologna and Rome, belonging to the owners Aimo Domenico and Carlo Fontana, before that.

The collection consists of a series of architectural drawings by Giuseppe Barberi (1746) mainly depicting design proposals for the Palazzo Reale in Milan. The drawings include detailed plans and elevations, as well as preliminary sketches and studies. 

The works demonstrate Barberi's mastery of classical architecture, seen in his use of symmetrical compositions, grand proportions, and intricate ornamentation. The drawings illustrate various stages of the Palazzo Reale's design, encompassing the development of the overall plan, individual rooms, facades, and surrounding gardens. The collection offers valuable perspectives on the architectural practices and aesthetic principles of the 18th century.
The curator of the collection is Rome, it is a private collection. The identity of the owner is unknown. The curator is responsible for the management and care of the collection.

The collection consists of a series of architectural drawings attributed to Giuseppe Barberi, dating from 1746. The drawings primarily focus on designs for the Palazzo Reale in Milan. They depict a variety of subjects, including villas, palaces, gardens, churches, and individual rooms within these grand structures.

Barberi's meticulous draftsmanship is evident in the detailed renderings of facades, floor plans, and elevations. The collection offers a valuable insight into the architectural trends and stylistic preferences of the period, showcasing Barberi's talent and his role in shaping the cityscape of Milan. The drawings are characterized by their elegant lines, precise measurements, and thoughtful composition, reflecting the high standards of architectural design in the 18th century.

The curator of the collection is Rome, a private collector.

The leaves contain drawings by Giuseppe Barberi, which primarily deal with architectural plans and studies. They depict a variety of buildings, including palaces, villas, churches, public buildings, and agricultural estates. The drawings are executed in different perspectives and scales and document both design ideas and detailed construction plans.

Studies for the Palazzo Reale in Milan are particularly frequent, illustrating Barberi's design process for this important building. The leaves offer insights into his architectural ideas, his working methods, and the artistic refinement of the Roman architect.

The drawing "Saturn Devouring One of His Children" is attributed to Parmigianino. The work was acquired by the Statens Museum for Kunst in Copenhagen in 1993 and is currently held in its Graphic Collection. The drawing was probably created between 1531 and 1535. It depicts the Roman god Saturn devouring one of his children on the back of another work, the study "Nessus". The technique of pen drawing with brown ink and wash is characteristic of Parmigianino. 

The drawing, which measures 220 x 193 mm, bears the inscription "Parmigianino" in the upper left corner above and the lower left corner beside the image field. It is part of the collection of the Statens Museum for Kunst in Copenhagen and is listed there under the number 92L726(NESSUS) 31A225 31D14.

Marzia Faietti dedicated a short contribution to the work in her publication "Amico Aspertini, Modena 1995". The drawing is also mentioned in the Gernsheim Catalogue and the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The custodian of the object is the Cambridge Fitzwilliam Museum, PD. 2-1994. It was previously in a private collection in London, owned by Philip Pouncey.

Further information about Franz Jakob Kreuter can be found in the publication "The Civil Engineer Franz Jakob Kreuter, Tradition and Modernity 1813 - 1889" by Chr. Hölz, published in 2003 in Munich and Berlin.

The drawing "God Separates Light from Darkness" dates from 1974 and is in the Hessian State Museum Darmstadt. It was formerly attributed to Francesco Solimena. The draughtsman is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue as J. Simane. It is a copy of the ceiling fresco cycle "God Separates Light from Darkness" by Michelangelo Buonarroti in the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican. The drawing is in chalk on pale blue paper and measures 129 x 174 mm.

The drawing was published in 1994 in the publication "Neapolitan Baroque Drawings" by J. Simane in Darmstadt.
The administrator of the Hessian State Museum Darmstadt is the Darmstadt Administrator. The museum opened in 1974.

The draftsman Wilhelm Tischbein, known as Goethe-Tischbein, Neapolitaner Tischbein, or simply Tischbein, created the drawing "The Crucifixion of Christ". The work was created in 1751 and is in the possession of the Kunsthalle Bremen. It is managed by the Kunsthalle Bremen. The drawing is executed on paper in chalk, with black and dark blue tones on white paper. The artist used both pen and brush. The dimensions are 345 x 210 mm and the drawing is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The list was revised by Stefan Morét.

The drawing "Preliminary Study for the Wall Painting Triumphal Procession of Emperor Zimisces" was created in Rome in 1660/1663. Guglielmo Borgognone created the drawing as a preliminary study for the wall painting in the Collegio Romano, Cappella Prima Primaria. The work is a preparatory drawing in ink on light beige paper and shows the composition of the "Triumphal Procession of Emperor Zimisces", which can be found in Rome in the Collegio Romano.  

The drawing is 170 x 185 mm in size and is in the possession of the Graphische Museum Düsseldorf. The provenance of the work can be traced back to Count D., who documented the drawing in his 1976 publication "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli".
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is FP 4472.

The pen drawing "Wedding Apparatus for Infante Philip of Spain" was created in 1738 and is the work of Ferdinando Fuga. The drawing, which is kept in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe F.N. in Rome (signature 1269), depicts an architectural design for a wedding apparatus. The format of the drawing is 530 x 749 mm. The drawing is executed in brown, gray, green, and yellow washes and in pen in brown, gray, green, and yellow. 

The pen drawing was presented in the publication "Ferdinando Fuga e l'architettura romana..." by E. Kieven (Rome 1988) in catalog number 73.

The curator of the Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe has published the drawing "S.r Matteo Polacco che à intagliato le Mie caricature". The work is by Pier Leone Ghezzi and was made by Ghezzi. The drawing depicts S.r Matteo Polacco engraving the artist's caricatures, which he had made for Cardinal Gio: Francesco Albani, onto copper. These caricatures were commissioned in 1749 by the Polish King and the Mediterranean King. Ghezzi describes the drawing's creation in 1749, when Matteo Federico Hermanin, who had come to Rome for the Holy Year, attended his music class.

The drawing is part of the "Drawing Art Miscellanea Rom 1750-1752" collection in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe, volume 2606. The drawing was created with ink (brown) and chalk (black) on a feather sheet (106 x 85 mm). The caption is a short text describing the drawing's creation and the roles of Matteo Polacco and the kings.
The property manager is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe 4708.

The drawing "Monsieur La Greniè Francese" is by Pier Leone Ghezzi and was created in 1751. It is part of a collection of drawings kept in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe in Rome. The drawing depicts Monsieur La Greniè Francese drawing the painted portrait of Am.e di Francia by Teniers. Ghezzi used brown ink and black chalk on paper, employing a pen as his drawing tool. The dimensions of the drawing are 116 x 82 mm. The drawing was created on March 15, 1751, as stated in the caption. 

The work is mentioned in various publications about Pier Leone Ghezzi and the drawings in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe collection, including "Un volume di disegni di Pier Leone Ghezzi" by Federico Hermanin and "I volti della storia nelle caricature della collezione di Pier Leone Ghezzi" by Antonella Pampalone.
The property manager is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe 4707.

The drawing "Ponte d'Augusto sull'Anione presso Vicovaro" is by Franz Caucig and was created between 1781 and 1787. The drawing is part of the collection of the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and was previously in the possession of the Narodna Galerija in Ljubljana. 

On the back of the drawing is a pen drawing in brown. In the upper right corner is the stamp "K.AKAD." and the Lugt stamp 1628. The drawing was mentioned in the publication "Franz Caucig: Italian Views" by J. Röll and K. Rozman (Petersberg 2018).

The drawing "Barazza Mercante di ogni genere di Galantarie" dates from 1751 and was created by Pier Leone Ghezzi. The sheet is executed in brown ink and black chalk on paper and measures 98 x 75 mm. The inscription on the sheet dates the work to December 27, 1751, and describes Barazza as "Mercante di ogni genere di Galantarie". 

The drawing was created by Pier Leone Ghezzi, a well-known Roman draughtsman of the 18th century. The work is part of a larger work published by Ghezzi under the title "Zeichenkunst". Ghezzi's drawings are known for their detailed depiction of Roman everyday scenes and characters.
The administrator of the property is the Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe, number 4724.

The German Doctor, Il Medico Tedesco, is a drawing by Pier Leone Ghezzi from 1750-1752. The drawing was created in Rome and is now in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe, Collection vol. 2606. The work is part of the Miscellanea Rom, a collection of graphic art. Pier Leone Ghezzi, the artist, also worked under the names Pietro Leone, Pier L., Pietro L., Pierleone and Leone Ghezzius, Petrus Leo. The drawing depicts a man and was drawn in brown ink and black chalk on paper.

The dimensions of the drawing are 118 x 89 mm. The caption reads: "Il Medico Tedesco p.seguitato dalli Medici di Roma e lo fecero metter prigione alli 2 di 7bre 1751. e ci stiede 8. giorni e poi lò fecero uscire con lo sfratto dà Roma." The work has been mentioned in various publications, including "Bollettino d'Arte" by Federico Hermanin (1907) and "‘700 disegnatore" by Antonella Pampalone (1997). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds a copy of the work.
The property manager is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe 4703.

The design for a base near the Quirinal is probably by Antonio da Sangallo (the Elder) and is in the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe of the Uffizi in Florence. The drawing on white paper with ink and pen shows the base with measurements. The architectural drawing is part of a collection of drawings dealing with Roman buildings. There are various inscriptions in Italian on the drawing that explain the dimensions and proportions of the base.

The inscriptions indicate that the measurements are in palms and that a palm is equal to 60 minuti. They also explain how the various parts of the base are divided into palms and minuti. The drawing is part of a collection of Roman buildings described by A. Bartoli in the book "I monumenti antichi di Roma nei disegni degli uffizi di firenze".
The curator of the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe is curator Florence Galleria degli Uffizi Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe U 1617 A.

The drawings are from the library of the Hertziana in Rome and were made by Pierre Mignard between 1640 and 1725. The album, which originally bore the title "Architectural Works and Monuments in Avignon and the County of Venaissin: Pen and Ink Drawings by Pierre Mignard, 1640 - 1725", contains detailed sketches of various buildings and monuments in the region. The depicted objects include, among others, the Porta Visani, the Fons Oppidi Pontis-Sorgiae, the Obeliscus Avenionensis, the Porta Insulana, and the Porta Balmarum.  

The drawings are executed in pen and ink on paper and usually bear the signature "P. Mignard Archit. Reg. Inven. Et delin." They are in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and were acquired by Ernst Steinmann in 1933. His bookplate can be found on the first endpaper, dated November 27, 1933.

The object custodian is the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The object is catalogued as Wa-MIG 4825-2850 and classified as "gr raro". The item was previously in a private collection in Rome before being acquired by Ernst Steinmann on November 27, 1933.

The drawings depict various buildings and monuments in Avignon and its surroundings, including the Porta Visani, the Fons Oppidi Pontis-Sorgiae, the Obeliscus Avenionensis, and the Porta Exterior Ptochotrophii Insulani.

The drawings are accompanied by detailed descriptions and signatures that point to Mignard's role as an architect and draftsman. The album also includes inscriptions from various buildings in Avignon. The drawings are executed in ink and pen on paper and are housed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The drawing "Design for a Wall Painting Cycle of the Stations of the Cross" by Carpoforo Tencalla dates from 1366 and depicts the beginning of the Stations of the Cross. It is executed on paper in chalk and brush in black and brown. The work is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was documented by Ch. Thiem in the catalogue "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" from 1977. Other drawings by Tencalla from the "Stations of the Cross" cycle are in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. These include "Christ Falls Beneath the Cross" (1371 and 1373), "Crucifixion of Christ" (1376), and "Resurrection of Christ" (1377).

The drawings by Carpoforo Tencalla are from the Staatsgalerie Graphische Sammlung Stuttgart and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome. They depict designs for a wall painting cycle on the theme of the Stations of the Cross. The drawings were made on paper with chalk and worked out with a brush in black and brown. The first drawings, including "Beginning of the Way of the Cross" (1366) and "Christ Falls under the Cross" (1371 and 1373), are in black and brown and depict the scene of the Way of the Cross.

Further drawings, such as "Crucifixion of Christ" (1376) and "Resurrection of Christ" (1377), are also in black and brown and deal with further Stations of the Cross. Tencalla's drawings are part of the important collection of Italian drawings from the 16th to 18th centuries of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart and were presented by Ch. The drawing "Design for a Wall Painting Cycle of the Stations of the Cross" is by Carpoforo Tencalla and is in the Graphic Collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart. The work is a preparatory drawing for a wall painting cycle and depicts the beginning of the Stations of the Cross. It is drawn on paper in chalk and executed in black and brown with a brush. The drawing, measuring 178 x 120 mm, is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. 

Other drawings by Carpoforo Tencalla for the Stations of the Cross cycle, also kept in the Graphic Collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, are "Christ Falls under the Cross" (1371 and 1373), "Crucifixion of Christ" (1376), and "Resurrection of Christ" (1377). These drawings, also drawn on paper in chalk and executed in black and brown with a brush, depict various stations of Christ's suffering and resurrection. They are also part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and were published by Ch. Thiem in his work "Italian Drawings 1500-1800".

The drawings are by Carpoforo Tencalla and depict designs for a fresco cycle on the theme of the Stations of the Cross. They are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The first drawing, "Beginning of the Way of the Cross," dates from 1366 and shows Christ on his way to the cross. It is executed on paper with chalk and brush in black and brown. The drawing "Christ Collapses under the Cross" was created in 1371 and depicts the Passion of Christ. Chalk and brush in black and brown were also used here.

The further drawings of the cycle depict the Crucifixion of Christ (1376), the Resurrection of Christ (1377) and further Stations of the Cross. All the drawings are executed on paper and designed with chalk and brush in black and brown. They were presented by Ch. Thiem in his publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" from 1977.

The drawings of the Stations of the Cross cycle are by Carpoforo Tencalla and are part of the Graphic Collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart. The drawings were designed by Tencalla for a wall painting cycle and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. They are executed on paper in chalk and brush. The first drawing, titled "Beginning of the Way of the Cross," was created in 1366 and depicts the crucifixion of Christ. The following drawings, "Christ Falls under the Cross" and "Crucifixion of Christ," were created in 1373 and 1376, respectively, and also deal with motifs from the Stations of the Cross cycle.

The last two drawings, "Christ Falls under the Cross" and "Resurrection of Christ," were created in 1377 and depict the climax and the end of the Stations of the Cross cycle. All the drawings were cataloged by Ch. Thiem in his publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" from 1977.

The drawing "Study of a Kneeling Bishop with Putto and Another Kneeling Figure" was created by Giorgio Gandini, an artist from the Baroque period. The drawing is executed on paper in red chalk and white gouache and measures 126 x 127 mm. It was formerly attributed to the painter Correggio, but was later attributed to Giorgio Gandini. The drawing "Monsieur Coscian Intagliatore di rame del Rè di Francia" by Pier Leone Ghezzi was created in 1750. The work was executed by Ghezzi in brown ink and black chalk on paper with a pen and has the dimensions 103 x 73 mm. The drawing is part of the "Zeichenkunst Miscellanea" collection in Rome, which was published between 1750 and 1752. 

The caption dates the drawing to April 25, 1750 and describes Monsieur Coscian as Intagliatore di rame del Rè di Francia. It also mentions that Coscian departed in the company of Monsieur Vandier and Federico Hermanin. The drawing has been examined and discussed in various publications, including "Bollettino d'Arte" and "Artisti e Mecenati".
The administrator of the property is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe 4690.

The drawing "Archibugiere famoso che mi à fatto 12 Archibugi à Mè Cav.r Ghezzi" by Pietro Riccardi dates from 1750 and depicts a famous Archibügiere. The work was commissioned by Cavaliere Ghezzi, who had commissioned the artist to create 12 Archibugi. The Archibügiere died in 1710, and Riccardi did not complete the portrait until 1750. The drawing is in brown and black ink and executed in pen, ink, and chalk on paper. It measures 101 x 70 mm and is in the possession of the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe in Rome.  

The drawing is part of a volume of Miscellanea from Rome from 1750-1752. It was published by Pier Leone Ghezzi and can be found in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe collection under number 2606. The drawing has been mentioned in various publications, including "Bollettino d'Arte" by Federico Hermanin (1907) and "Artisti e Mecenati" by Antonella Pampalone (1996).

Published by the Keeper of Prints and Drawings of the British Museum on June 14, 1856, this work is a drawing by the Italian artist Parmigianino. The brown pen drawing depicts two fighting men in front of a tent. It consists of four sketches for a kneeling Madonna. The drawing measures 153 x 126 mm and bears the inventory number 11 F 45 31 A (+92 23) 41 A 19 1 A.E. Popham, Drawings of Parmigianino, 3 Bde., 1971, Kat. 189. 

The reverse side of the drawing shows studies of two male half-figures, heads, hands, and a leg. The studies are numbered 31 A 22 5 (+31) 31 A 22 1 (+32+72) 31 A 22 45 (+72) and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the British Museum's Department of Prints and Drawings is based in London. The object is catalogued under the signature 1856-6-14-2 and is managed in two parts, r and v.

The draftsman Il Parmigianino, also known as Francesco Mazzola or Francesco Mazzola, Girolamo Francesco Maria Mazzuoli, Girolamo Francesco Maria Parmigianino, created the pen drawing "Two Fighting Men Before a Tent". The drawing, consisting of four sketches, served as the basis for a kneeling Madonna. The work is made on paper in brown and measures 153 x 126 mm. It is in the collections of the British Museum in London and bears the inventory number 11 F 45 31 A (+92 23) 41 A 19 1 A.E. Popham described the drawing in his publication "Drawings of Parmigianino", 3 vols., 1971, under number 189.

On the back of the drawing are further studies of two male half-figures, heads, hands, and a leg. These studies are also numbered 31 A 22 5 (+31), 31 A 22 1 (+32+72), 31 A 22 45 (+72) and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Department of Prints and Drawings at the British Museum in London manages the object under the number 1856-6-14-2 r. The corresponding curator's number for the reverse side of the object is 1856-6-14-2 v.

The caption indicates that Ricci traveled from Rome to Florence on March 29, 1751, accompanied by Marchese Aldobrandini. 

The drawing is part of the "Disegni Miscellanea Rom 1750-1752" collection in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe, volume 2606. Further information about the drawing and Pier Leone Ghezzi can be found in publications by Federico Hermanin (1907) and Antonella Pampalone (1997).

Salcindio Tiseio also contributed to the work. The work is an interior view and belongs to the genre of drawings. It is a pen drawing measuring 219 x 123 mm. The work is listed in the Gernsheim Catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under number 48 C 14 31.

The drawing "Male Nude, Running" is attributed to Domenico Fetti and dates from 1829. The inventory or collection number is Ratjen R 29 v. The Vaduz Foundation is managed by the Vaduz Foundation. The drawing is executed in black chalk and wash in pen and ink on paper. It measures 414 x 274 mm and belongs to series 31 A (+89) in the Gernsheim catalogue list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. 

There is also the possibility that the drawing is by Francesco Vanni, a follower of Domenico Fetti.
The administrator of the Vaduz Foundation is Ratjen R 29 v.
The image depicts a nude human figure, representing the beauty and perfection of the human body.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection. It comes from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and bears the inventory number 135604_post. The photograph was donated to the art museum by the Gernsheims on March 21, 2011.

The drawing "Reclining Man, Supporting Himself with His Left Arm" was published by the administrator of the Worms Foundation Kunsthaus Heylshof. It is a work by Filippo Angeli. The execution of the drawing is attributable to Filippo Teodoro de Llaño Lagno, Filippo Teodoro de Liagno, Filippo Teodoro de Liano, Filippo Teodoro de Llaño, Filippo Teodoro de Llanos or Filippo Teodoro de Filippo Angeli. The drawing is a pen drawing on paper measuring 57 x 86 mm. It is part of the collection of the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom, and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue.
The property manager is the Worms Foundation Kunsthaus Heylshof 4/W 96.

The drawing "Fantasy Interior" by Giovanni Battista Piranesi dates from 1840 and was published in the British Museum in London. The work was produced by Piranesi himself and signed by Salcindio Giovanni Battista Tiseio. The drawing is a fantasy architecture and depicts an interior with chalk, pen and brown wash. The dimensions of the drawing are 382 x 255 mm. 

Further information about the drawing can be found in the Gernsheim catalogue list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The custodian of the object is the British Museum Department of Prints and Drawings in London. The object was acquired by the museum on March 14, 1840. The inventory number is 159.

The drawing "Saint Elizabeth of Hungary" comes from the Ubaldini Collection of the Biblioteca Comunale in Urbania. It is attributed to Domenico Peruzzini and is in the possession of the administrators of Urbania. The drawing was made in Peruzzini's workshop. The work is executed in ink, chalk, and quill in a wash technique, with the ink in brown and the chalk in black. 

The format of the drawing is 278 x 162 mm and was already presented in the publication "Disegni della Biblioteca Comunale di Urbania. La Collezione Ubaldini" by M. Cellini from 1999, Volume 2, catalogue number 455. It is in the possession of the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Urbania Biblioteca Comunale Collezione Ubaldini is Urbania. The administrator can be reached at the address II, 123. 485.
The image depicts Saint Elizabeth of Hungary.

Published in the British Museum, London, in the Department of Prints and Drawings. The work is by Claude Lorrain, also known as Claude Gellée or Lorenese, Claude. The bust itself is in the Villa Albani. The drawing was made in pen and red ink on paper and measures 347 x 232 mm. 

The drawing is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was mentioned in a catalogue by Jean Sampson, "Drawings and Engravings in the Topham Collection at Eton College", 1974.

The painting "Street with Village Bridge" was created in 203 by Friedrich Georg Weitsch. It is a drawing executed in various techniques: watercolor, chalk, and pen, the latter used in hatched techniques. The work measures 328 x 487 mm and is in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Leipzig Museum of Fine Arts is the NI 203.

Published in 1918 by the Keeper of the British Museum, Department of Prints and Drawings, London. The dimensions of the drawing are 120 x 109 mm. The drawing is catalogued as 48 C 14 31 : 25 I 24 4 and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The drawing "Standing Martyr with Book" was made by Benozzo Gozzoli. The pen drawing was created as part of the circle around the artist Sandro Botticelli. The drawing is executed in silverpoint and white lead on laid paper. The support was primed with a brush in brown and white. The dimensions are 154 x 82 mm. The drawing is part of the Graphic Collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, signature C 63/1153.

The work was presented in the publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem, Stuttgart 1977, under number 376. The drawing is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection C 63/1153, is based in Stuttgart.

The drawing "Circe gives the companions of Odysseus drink" was published in 1895 by the Keeper of Prints and Drawings at the London British Museum. The drawing is attributed to Parmigianino. It is by Il Parmigianino (Mazzoli, Francesco) and is a copy of the work "Circe gives the companions of Odysseus drink" from the Florence Galleria degli Uffizi. The drawing is executed in blue paper with pen and watercolor. It measures 244 x 199 mm. The drawing is part of the British Museum collection and bears the inventory number 94 I 16 31 A 11 (+4) 41 C 32 2 46 C 21 5 (BOW) 25 FF 42 2.  

The drawing is documented in the Gernsheim Catalogue, Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom.
The curator of the London British Museum, Department of Prints and Drawings, made the entry numbered 749 on September 15, 1895.
The image depicts Odysseus on the island of Circe. Odysseus, encircled by a large, mythical dragon, stands as a figure with a jug or a cup in his hand.

Permission for publication was granted by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The curator of Windsor Castle, the Royal Library, holds the object RL 7204. It is a pen drawing by the artist Leonello Spada. The dimensions of the drawing are 308 x 210 mm and it is part of the Gernsheim catalogue under the number 32 A 5 : 11 P 31 21. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has a catalogue of the Gernsheim.

The work is part of the collection of the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe in Rome and can be found in the Gernsheim catalog list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome under number 31 A 23 51.

The drawing "Study for a Forward-Charging Figure" is attributed to Stefano della Bella. It was made in 1631. The work is an example of the artist's drawing skills and was created on paper with a pen. It was made by Calderi, who is also the draughtsman. The tracing is based on a statue in the Albertinum in Dresden. The drawing is executed in ink on paper with a pen and measures 385 x 497 mm. It is part of the 61 F (PALAZZO CHIGI) and 25 F 24 61 E (ROMA) collections. Jean Sampson mentions the drawing in his work "Drawings and Engravings in the Topham Collection at Eton College".
The property manager is Eton Eton College Topham Collection B.m. 7.

A holy priest martyr is the subject of this drawing by Giovanni Paolo Melchiori, held in the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe in Rome. It measures 338 x 212 mm and is part of the Gernsheim catalogue list of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The art historian Stefan Morét has recorded the drawing in his list.

The curator of the London British Museum, Department of Prints and Drawings, registered the object on July 22, 1989, under the number 46 r. On the same day, the object was also registered with the curator under the number 46 v.

The drawing is on paper with pen and ink and measures 497 x 384 mm. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was described by Jean Sampson in his 1974 publication "Drawings and Engravings in the Topham Collection at Eton College".

The study of a man with a sword and shield in profile was drawn by Giovanni Paolo Melchiori. The drawing "Front of Madonna, Study" is by Michelangelo Buonarroti and is in the Cabinet des Dessins of the Musée National du Louvre in Paris. The work was made in 1475 and is in chalk and pen on paper in the format 11 F 42. The back of the drawing is designated as "recto," indicating that it is the front of the original drawing. The drawing is part of the collection of Ch. de Tolnay and was documented in his work "Corpo dei disegni di Michelangelo."

The Hertziana Library in Rome houses the drawing.

The drawing is a characteristic representation of the artist's graphic art, executed in ink, pencil, and pen.

The drawing is in black and gray wash and measures 178 x 248 mm. It is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and has been mentioned in earlier publications by experts such as E. Sack.

The back of the object is blank. There is a publication by Dieter Graf, "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri, Kunstmuseum Düsseldorf III,5, Düsseldorf 1995, No. 972", and a mention in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, regarding this work.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf KA (FP) is the curator of the collection.

The drawing "Studies for Perseus and Andromeda" was made by Marco da Faenza, an artist from Marco Marchetti's workshop. The work was created in 1922 and is in the Graphic Collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart. The drawing is on paper in ink and red chalk, and is drawn with a pen. The ink is brown and light brown, the red chalk is also used in various tones. The format of the drawing is 155 x 250 mm. 

The drawing was previously presented in the publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem from 1977.
The State Gallery in Stuttgart manages the Graphic Collection C 1922/63.
The image depicts Perseus in the moment he defeats Medusa.

The photograph belongs to the "g-art" category and is viewed in the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings in the context of drawings.

The drawing "Standing Woman in a Long Dress" is by Stefano della Bella and was created between 1635 and 1636. The work is in the possession of the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe in Rome and was published there by the curator F.C. Bella. The drawing is executed in ink and pencil on paper and measures 150 x 88 mm. 

The pen drawing depicts a woman standing in a long dress. It is part of the collection "Disegni di Stefano della Bella" and was published in 1976 by M. Catelli in Rome. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds the drawing under catalog number 31 A 72 41 D 27.
The administrator of the property is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe F.C.
The picture shows a woman enveloped in a robe.

The drawing "Hippolyt as Horse Tamer" (Design for a Tapestry) by Pirro Ligorio is from the collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection. The work was acquired from a private collection in 1959 and was previously owned by the Ziegler family. The drawing is a preparatory sketch for a tapestry and depicts Hippolyt as a horse tamer. 

The drawing was made with brown ink on paper and is 318 x 212 mm in size. The upper right corner is torn. It is part of the collection of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection and was featured in the publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem, Stuttgart 1977.

The object manager of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphische Sammlung, is C 63/1182. The work was acquired in 1959 and was previously in a private collection. The last private owner before the purchase by the Staatsgalerie was Ernst Ziegler.

It is the front side of a study for the clothing and feet of the Tiburtine Sibyl, which Passeri created for his wall painting in the Santa Maria in Aracoeli in Rome. The drawing is executed in chalk on grayish-green paper and shows the preparations for the depiction of the Sibyl.

The drawing is 422 x 280 mm in size and is located in the Kunstmuseum Düsseldorf. It was described by Dieter Graf in his publication "The Drawings of Giuseppe Passeri" and is also listed in the catalog of the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The curator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is KA (FP) and it is the recto.

The drawing was made in brown ink on paper and depicts three adults and a child. The dimensions are 154 x 106 mm. The pen drawing is part of the collection of the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe and was documented by M. Catelli in the work "Disegni di Stefano della Bella" in Rome 1976, Cat. 21.

The drawing is in the collection of the State Graphic Collection Munich. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and the Museum in Hamburg also hold works by Giambattista and Domenico Tiepolo.
