The map of the Val di Chiana was published in 1814 by Niccolò Gamurini, an Italian artist. It is located in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale in Florence and is part of the collection of the possessions of the Crown Estate in the Val di Chiana. The drawing, executed in watercolor and pen, is 245 x 323 mm in size. Gamurini also created a series of drawings depicting views and floor plans of houses and estates in the region. These works, also executed in watercolor and pen and each measuring 323 x 245 mm, include among others views and location plans of buildings in Arezzo, Frassineto, Montecchio, Creti, Chinacce, Dolciano, Acquaviva, the Fattoria dell'Abbadia, Fojano, Bettole, Font'a Ronco, the Fattoria del Pozzo, Tegoleto and Ponte della Nave.

Furthermore, Gamurini drew the Fabbriche della Chiusa, the view and floor plan of which were also created in watercolor and pen on paper measuring 323 x 245 mm.

The manuscript was produced in 1760 by Johannes Grevembroch and comes from the Gradenigo Dolfin Library in the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice. The work is watercolored and contains drawings of washbasins and other ornate fittings from Venetian palaces and churches. Among the depicted washbasins are those in the Rosso Marin's residence, the Palazzo Ducale, the Santo Stefano church, and the refectory of the Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari church.

The drawings also include those of a fireplace in the Palazzo Ducale with the coat of arms of Doge Agostino Barbarigo, a two-tiered marble basin on eight columns in Santo Stefano, and a wall basin with the coat of arms of Doge Girolamo Priuli from the Palazzo Ducale. The drawings are detailed and offer insights into the ornate interior decoration of Venetian buildings from the 15th and 16th centuries. The manuscript is inscribed with a dedication to Pietro Gradenigo and Giovanni Grevembroch, highlighting their merits.

The drawings are of high quality and detailed, offering a valuable insight into the art and architecture of the Venetian Renaissance.

The drawings are detailed and show the architecture and decoration of Venetian houses and public buildings in the 15th and 16th centuries. Many drawings are labeled with descriptions that indicate the location, owner, or date of the buildings and details. The manuscript offers a valuable insight into the art and architecture of Renaissance Venice.

The manuscript is a valuable testament to the art and architecture of 16th and 17th-century Venice.

The illustrated manuscript originates from the National Central Library in Florence. It contains drawings by the artist and architect Francesco di Giorgio Martini. The drawings primarily focus on engineering and military architecture, depicting various devices and structures such as fountains, fortifications, water pumps, cranes, and lifting mechanisms. 

The collection also includes drawings of ships, a dovecote, and figures, including Allegories. The drawings are executed in black ink on parchment, with some in mixed media using metalpoint. The manuscript is documented in the book "Francesco di Giorgio Martini and the Renaissance in Siena 1450-1500" by L. Bellosi.

The drawings, primarily executed on parchment with ink and sometimes with a metallic stylus, illustrate a variety of subjects related to engineering, architecture, and civil defense. They include designs for bridges, fortifications, waterworks, cranes, and various lifting devices. The artist, Francesco di Giorgio Martini, masterfully portrays both theoretical concepts and practical applications of mechanics. The drawings, part of the Biblioteca Hertziana collection in Rome, offer valuable insights into the technical knowledge and innovative spirit of Renaissance engineering.

Among the depicted designs are intricate water wheels, hydraulic systems, and innovative siege weapons. Martini's meticulous attention to detail is evident in his representations of gears, pulleys, levers, and other mechanical components. His sketches also demonstrate his understanding of human anatomy and animal locomotion, as seen in drawings of workers operating machinery and animals powering devices. The collection provides a fascinating glimpse into the creative mind of a Renaissance engineer who combined artistic talent with a profound understanding of scientific principles.
The administrator of the object is Florenz Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale. The address is Palatino 767.

Graf in his publication "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli" from 1976 and is now located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The manuscript "Opus Architectonicum" by Francesco Borromini, published in 1646, contains a comprehensive documentation of his architectural work. Among the preserved drawings are sketches and plans for the Casa dei Filippini, including the facade, the ground floor plan, the interior layout of the main hall, and the design of the courtyard. 

Further drawings, dated after 1647, depict various aspects of the Casa dei Filippini, such as details of the portal, the staircase, and the fountain. These designs, possibly by anonymous assistants or followers of Borromini, provide valuable insights into the evolution of the project and the construction process. Notably, a set of drawings for the Palazzo Pamphilj, including a cross-section of the Salone, showcases Borromini's architectural vision in a different context.
The archivist of the Congregation of the Oratory of Rome in Santa Maria in Vallicella manages manuscript c. II. 6. The Vatican Apostolic Library holds manuscript vat. lat. fol. 192.

The image depicts a representation of the Casa dei Filippini, a complex of buildings that includes an oratory, a sacristy, a conventual church, and various interior spaces such as a corridor, a studiolo, and a library. The drawing shows both floor plans and cross-sections of the various building parts and focuses on architectural details such as portals, windows, and balustrades.

The manuscript Opus Architectonicum by Francesco Borromini, created between 1646 and 1647, contains detailed drawings and designs for the Casa dei Filippini in Rome. It includes plans, cross-sections, and views of the building, including the main portal, the courtyard, the refectory, and the library. The drawings demonstrate Borromini's characteristic architectural style, characterized by dynamic forms, complex facades, and the use of light and shadow.

Further drawings held by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome come from Borromini's workshop and from anonymous artists. They document the development of the Casa dei Filippini project after Borromini's death and provide insights into the building's realization. The drawings show, among other things, facade elevations, details such as window niches and balustrades, and the reconstruction of the south wing in the second courtyard.

The archivist of the Archivio della Congregazione dell'Oratorio di Roma at Santa Maria in Vallicella preserves the manuscript "ms. c. II. 6". In addition, the Vatican Apostolic Library holds the manuscript "vat. lat. fol. 192".

Published in the Archivio della Congregazione dell'Oratorio di Roma a Santa Maria in Vallicella, manuscript c. II. 6, Francesco Borromini's Opus Architectonicum MS (J. Connors, Opus Architectonicum, Milan 1998), is a collection of 79 sheets with 36 drawings. Dating from 1646-1647, the work offers a comprehensive overview of the architect's architectural ideas and designs. Among the drawings are studies for the Casa dei Filippini, including detailed plans, sections, and elevations.

The manuscript also contains designs for other projects, such as the Oratorio di San Filippo Neri, the Palazzo Pamphilj, and a fountain for the Casa dei Filippini. The drawings demonstrate Borromini's distinctive architectural style, characterized by its dynamism, theatricality, and innovative use of light and space. They provide valuable insights into the creative process of one of the most important architects of the Italian Baroque.

The curator of the collection is located in the archive of the Congregazione dell'Oratorio di Roma in Santa Maria in Vallicella. There, the manuscript c. II. 6 is housed. An additional copy is held in the Vatican Library, where it is designated as vat. lat. fol. 192.

The fortress of L'Aquila degli Abruzzi was documented in a drawing before its conversion into an army barracks. The pen and ink drawing is by J. Eberhardt and is part of the series "The Fortress of L'Aquila degli Abruzzi and its Architect Pyrrhus Aloisius Scrivà". The drawing was created in L'Aquila in 1870 and is archived at the Istituto Storico e di Cultura dell'Arma del Genio Abruzzese. It depicts the overall complex, the floor plan, the southeast facade, and a cross-section of the fortress.

In addition to Eberhardt's drawing, there are four further architectural drawings in the archive of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. These anonymous drawings also show detailed floor plans of the individual floors of the fortress: basement, ground floor, upper floor, and roof terraces. All the drawings are in a comparable size (32 x 44.5 cm) and bear the same markings.

The administrator of the property is the Rom Istituto Storico e di Cultura dell'Arma del Genio.

The Madonna with the John the Baptist is a preparatory drawing in the field of graphic arts. The drawing was made by Bartolomeo Schidone on paper with red chalk and measures 214 x 172 mm. The work is in the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement at Chatsworth House. 

The first known owner of the drawing was the Italian bishop Matteo Marchetti, who kept it in his private collection. Subsequently, the Madonna with the John the Baptist came into the possession of Lord Summers, who kept it in his private collection in Arezzo. As the third previous owner, William, the second Duke of Devonshire, came into possession of the drawing and kept it in his private collection in London. In 1717, the drawing entered the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement at Chatsworth House, where it has remained to this day.

The curator of the Chatsworth House private collection is the organization Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. The painting is currently owned by the fourth previous owner. Previously, it was owned by William (Duke, 2) Devonshire, who owned it between 1710 and 1716. Before him, it was owned by Lord Summers from London. From 1698, the painting belonged to the private collection of Bishop Matteo Marchetti from Arezzo. 

The first owner of the painting was Padre Sebastiano Resta.

Curator Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi 599 E v, a chalk drawing on black, was traditionally attributed to Michelangelo Buonarroti. The earlier attribution was by Francesco Ubertini. Paola Barocchi later attributed the drawing to Michelangelo. The drawing depicts a half-figure study of a young woman in profile, as well as two female heads in profile. It measures 339 x 236 mm.

The drawing is part of the collection of the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi in Florence. It was verbally identified by Alexander Perrig on June 21, 2006. The execution is attributed to Antonio Mini. The work has been mentioned in earlier publications, including by Paola Barocchi in her work "Michelangelo and His School" (Florence 1962) and by Ch. de Tolnay in his "Corpus of Drawings..." (Novara 1975-80). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has information about the drawing.

The pen drawings held by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome are from the estate of the administrator of the Fanoer Library, Federiciana. They were created between 1741 and 1800 and depict designs for the decoration of the Theatro della Fortuna in Fano. The drawings include designs for balconies, stage decorations, architectural decorations, a ground plan of the basement, wall decorations, stage machinery, and stage room machinery. 

The drawings also show various designs for the theater's audience seating. Some of the drawings exist in multiple versions, suggesting that the administrator experimented with various ideas before settling on a final design. The drawings are valuable documents for the history of the theater in Fano and offer insights into the artistic conceptions of the 18th century.

The Casa Sangallo is depicted in partial elevations and floor plans, which, in combination with other drawings of the Palazzo Sacchetti and Rome, offer insights into the architecture and urban planning of the time. The work was published in the volume "The Architectural Drawings [...], vol. IV" edited by C. L. Frommel and G. Schelbert. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome is the owner of the drawing.

The painting is in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was previously in a private collection in Rome, since 1895/1896 in the Glingler collection, Karl.

The photograph dates from 1953/1956 and depicts Albrecht Dürer's portrait of Oswolt Krell. It was produced as a photolithograph by F. Bruckmann A.-G. in Munich. The photograph is numbered 236 and is located in the Pinakothek in Munich.

The triptych by Oswald Krell, created in 1499, is a work by the famous painter Albrecht Dürer. The painting is in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich and is part of the Bavarian State Painting Collections. The triptych consists of three parts: the central panel, the side wings, and the Krell family coat of arms. The central panel depicts a portrait of Oswald Krell and measures 49.6 x 39 cm. The two side wings each show the coats of arms of the Krell and von Esendorf families.

Photographs of the triptych are in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The first publication of the triptych is from 1980 and can be found in Anzelewsky's work "Dürer, Albrecht".
The administrator of the Bavarian State Painting Collections Alte Pinakothek in Munich is the Munich Administrator.

The photograph itself is a rarity and was produced using the photomechanical process. It was fully adhered and bears the stamp of the Royal Bavarian Directorate of State Galleries in Munich.

In the Church of San Giacomo Maggiore in Bologna is the Cappella Bentivoglio chapel on the south wall. The wall painting "Throned Madonna with Giovanni II Bentivoglio and his Family" (Pala Bentivoglio) was created by Lorenzo Costa the Elder in 1488.

The panel painting "Throned Madonna with Giovanni II Bentivoglio and his Family" (Pala Bentivoglio) was created in 1488. The work by the painter Lorenzo Costa the Elder is located in the Cappella Bentivoglio chapel on the south wall of the San Giacomo Maggiore church in Bologna. The inscription on the painting dates it to August 2, 1488, and reads "Me patriam ed dulces cara cum coniuge natos comendo precibus Virgo beata tuis MCCCCLXXXVIII Augusti Laurentus Costa faciebat".

The painting depicts the enthroned Madonna, Giovanni II Bentivoglio, Lord of Bologna, and his family. Among those depicted are Alessandro, Ermete, Annibale, Anton Galeazzo, Ginevra Sforza, Bianca, Francesca, Violante, Laura, Isotta, Eleonora Bentivoglio. The tempera on canvas panel painting has been studied and published by various art historians and scientists.

The self-portrait of the Italian painter Domenico Morelli dates from 1880/1885. The oil painting on canvas depicts the artist in a quiet moment of self-reflection. The self-portrait has already been exhibited in various exhibitions, including the Domenico Morelli exhibition in 1907 in Rome and the Italian Art exhibition in 1937 in Berlin.
The custodian of the objects is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome. The objects were donated to the gallery in 1905.

The painting "Copy after Portrait of Pope Leo X. with the Cardinals Giuliano de'Medici and Luigi de'Rossi" is by the Florentine painter Giuliano Bugiardini. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 157 x 117.5 cm. The work was donated to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome by the Torlonia family in 1982. Previously, it was in a private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome. The inscription on the painting provides information about its origin and history. It reads: "Copiato dall'originale di Raffaele per mano di Giuliano Bugiardini / Per comando del Card: Innocenzo Cybo, di cui è ritratto / la Testa con la Barba".

Vasari's biography of Giuliano Bugiardini mentions the copy, which was made after a painting by Raphael and commissioned by Cardinal Innocenzo Cybo, whose portrait is depicted in the painting. The work was brought from Massa to Rome in 1729. Further information can be found in the catalogue of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini by Mochi and Vodret (2008).

The custodian of the object is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The object was donated in 1982 by the Torlonia family. Prior to that, the object was in a private collection of the Torlonia family in Rome.

The painting "Fall of the Damned" by Hieronymus Bosch is located in the Doge's Palace in Venice. The work was created between 1500 and 1504 and belongs to a cycle of four depictions of the afterlife. The four paintings, each oil on wood, depict the fall of the damned, hell, the ascent of the saved into paradise, and heavenly paradise.  

"Fall of the Damned," "Hell," "Ascent of the Saved into Paradise," and "Heavenly Paradise" are each 88.5 x 41.5 cm in size and are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The painting "Fall of the Damned" was first cataloged in 1970 by P. Reuterswärd in his publication on Hieronymus Bosch.

In the Doge's Palace in Venice is the painting "Fall of the Damned" by Hieronymus Bosch. The work dates from the period between 1500 and 1504 and is part of a cycle of four depictions of the afterlife. The other three paintings in the cycle are "Hell", "Ascent of the Saved into Paradise" and "Heavenly Paradise". All four paintings are oil paintings on wood and measure 88.5 x 41.5 cm each. They are located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The cycle of the four depictions of the afterlife was probably created by Hieronymus Bosch between 1500 and 1504. The artist was known for his detailed and gloomy depictions of the afterlife. The paintings in the Doge's Palace are important testimonies to the artist's work and provide insights into his vision of the earthly and otherworldly realm.

The painting "Piazza Montecavallo and Quirinal Palace" was created in Rome in 1683. It is a tempera painting on parchment, measuring 26.4 x 47.3 cm. The work is by the painter Gaspar Adriaensz van Wittel, also known as "Gaspar van Wittel" or "Il Bamboccio". The painting depicts the Palazzo del Quirinale in Rome, as well as the human-animal group of the Dioscuri.

The painting is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. It was acquired in 1895 through a gift from the Odescalchi family. The depiction of the Palazzo del Quirinale served as a model for other works, including a painting by Wittel that is in the Galleria Colonna. The Dioscuri group forms the basis for a study by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret, which was published in the catalog of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini.
The curator of the "Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini" is a gift from the Odescalchi family dating back to 1895.

In Rome, in the Palazzo della Valle, on the piano nobile, there is a hall with a coffered ceiling decorated with depictions of Sibyls. In addition, information can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, which illuminates various aspects of the painting, such as the "Crucifixion with the Saints Bruno of Querfurt and Andrew" and the scenes "Saint Bruno of Querfurt Passes the Fire Test" and "The Miracle of Nicaea of Saint Andrew".

A polyptych by Michele di Matteo da Bologna is located in the Church of Sant'Elena in Venice. The work, signed "MICHAEL MATHEI DA BONONIA," was cataloged by F. The polyptych consists of several panels, including a Seated Madonna with four angels, paintings of Saint Lucia, Saint Helena, Saint Mary Magdalene, and Saint Catherine of Alexandria. 

Other panels depict the Crucifixion, a cycle of Church Fathers, a cycle of Evangelists, Christ, Saints, and the Legend of the Cross in the predella. The paintings are oil on wood and have the dimensions 142 x 63 cm (Seated Madonna), 142 x 82 cm (Saints), and 111 x 64 cm (Crucifixion).
The administrator in Venice is the Galleria dell'Accademia.

A study by F. Zeri from 1992, published in the "Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom", states that the work can be found in Messina, at the Museo Regionale.
The administrator of the Messina Regional Museum of Messina is Messina.
A black-and-white photograph from 1976 shows a full view of the BAS NA Camp. The image is restricted.

The painting is located in the Assunta Cathedral in Sant'Agata de' Goti. It was created between 1601 and 1700 and depicts a scene from the life of Saint Charles Borromeo. The painting is an oil on canvas work. The artwork measures 11 H by 4 (+3) units in width. Further information about the painting can be found at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A painting in the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio, Umbria, depicts the portrait of Marsilia Gioia. The administrator of the Palazzo Ducale published the work around 1651/1675. Further information about the painting can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale company.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi's work from 1381.175.tif was named bhex-2022-35-175 on July 3, 2023. The color photograph shows the complete artwork with frame, which was used for rights clearance. Roberto Sigismondi commissioned the artwork as part of order 35/2022.

A painting created around 1601/1650 by an administrator of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio depicts the portrait of Erudito. The oil painting on canvas has some missing sections. The dimensions of the painting are 61 x 2.

The catalog number is (ERUDITO) 11 (+54) 41 A 71 22 49 M 32 48 C 24 49 MM 32 23 U 22 49 L 51 49 L 62. The painting is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is called Gubbio Palazzo Ducale.

A digital photograph, part of the O.C.S.A. Arezzo-43-S.-Flora-e-Lucilla collection, is designated bhex-2022-14-037 and was taken in Tuscany in 2022. The photograph shows a full view and was commissioned by Marcello Leotta in November 2021. The usage rights are divided. 

The color of the photograph is "Leotta" and it was digitized on September 27, 2022.

In the monastery church Chiesa di Badia Sante Flora e Lucilla in Arezzo, there is a painting by Giorgio Vasari. The Coronation of Mary with Saints, created around 1567/1570, was painted on canvas in oil. The dimensions of the painting are 73 A x 79 2 (+3) 73 E x 77 1 11 H (DONATUS) 11 H (FRANCIS) 11 HH (CATHERINE OF SIENA) 11 HH (APOLLONIA) 11 HH (AGATHA) 11 HH (URSULA) 11 HH (CATHERINE) 11 HH (LUCY) 11 HH (MARGARET) 11 HH (MARY MAGDALENE). The work has been studied in various publications, including "Le Opere di Vasari in Arezzo" by G.F. Gamurrini, "Giorgio Vasari - Der literarische Nachlass" by K. Frey and H.-W. Frey, and "Vasari e la Maniera moderna" by A. Cecchi.

Further research can be found in the works "Arte in terra d'Arezzo. Il Cinquecento" by L. Fornasari and A. Giannotti, and "Recycling, Renaissance Style: Hybridity and Giorgio Vasari's Pieve Altarpieces" by S. Cornelison. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds documents and materials related to the painting.

A photograph shows the family chapel in Marburg on B 27 road. The photograph is numbered 27.277/4 and was taken in 2002. The black-and-white photo is from the Gloc collection and was taken as part of a KHI photo campaign in 2000. The campaign focused on family chapels, and this photograph shows a general view of the chapel, which was closed at the time.

The painting "Coronation of Mary with Saints" is located in the monastery church Chiesa di Badia Sante Flora e Lucilla in Arezzo. It was painted by Giorgio Vasari around 1567/1570 on oil on canvas. The work measures 73 A 79 2 (+3) 73 E 77 1 11 H (DONATUS) 11 H (FRANCIS) 11 HH (CATHERINE OF SIENA) 11 HH (APOLLONIA) 11 HH (AGATHA) 11 HH (URSULA) 11 HH (CATHERINE) 11 HH (LUCY) 11 HH (MARGARET) 11 HH (MARY MAGDALENE). 

The painting has been mentioned in various publications, including "Le Opere di Vasari in Arezzo" by G.F. Gamurrini, "Giorgio Vasari - Der literarische Nachlass" by K. Frey and H.-W. Frey, "Vasari e la Maniera moderna" by A. Cecchi and "Recycling, Renaissance Style" by S. Cornelison.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi's work from 1381.174.tif was taken in color on July 3, 2023, under the designation bhex-2022-35-174. An inscription on the top edge of the picture field reads "JULIUS GABRIELLIS / ORATOR.EGREGIUS.FLOR.AN:MDL".

The portrait of Giulio Gabrielli is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale published a portrait of Antonio Di Vittorio Concioli around 1746/1755. A painting in the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio depicts Leonardo Porcelli dei Conti di Carbonana. The portrait was created around 1646/1655 by the administrator of the Palazzo Ducale. The painting is part of the Palazzo Ducale collection in Gubbio and is part of Umbrian art. It is documented in the catalog of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is Gubbio Palazzo Ducale.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi's work from 1381.178.tif was taken in color on July 3, 2023, under the designation bhex-2022-35-178. The painting, dated 1646/1655, depicts a portrait of a man in armor. It is an oil painting on canvas. The work by the administrator of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio is affected by paint loss. The dimensions of the painting are 61 B x 11 H x 49 L cm. Further details relate to the dimensions in the categories D (26 cm), A (42 cm) and C (16 cm).

The provenance of the painting is connected to the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A photograph of Ravenna, taken by Marco on September 27, 2021. The photograph is titled P50/2 and may be a black and white image. It shows a panoramic view of Ravenna, which is however blocked.

Antonio Maria Valsalva, a physician and professor at the University of Bologna, is the subject of a painting from the 17th or 18th century. The portrait of Antonio Maria Valsalva was painted in oil on canvas by an unknown artist. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was exhibited there from September 27th to October 1st, 2021.
The administrator is the Bologna Università di Bologna.

The church Chiesa di Santa Maria di Loreto in Petralia Soprana houses a painting of Saints Cosmas and Damian, which is attached to the left arm of the cross. The painting is from Sicily and was created between 1601 and 1700. The image is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
A black and white photograph from 1976 shows the overall view of the BAS NA Camp. The entire facility is fenced off in the photograph.

In Sant'Agata de' Goti, in the Duomo Assunta Cathedral, there is a Campanian Madonna. The painting dates from between 1701 and 1800 and depicts the Madonna delle Grazie. It is an oil painting on canvas, measuring 11 F 5 (+3) 11 T 6. 

The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome is responsible for provenance research.

A rare photograph by Alinari Anderson, taken before 1957, is available as an albumen print in the size 4066. The photograph is fully mounted and shows yellowing, silvering, and wave patterns. A fingerprint is also visible. The back shows a wavy condition, damaged edges, and a yellow spot. 

The stamp is missing.

The painting "The Ballroom" from the Venetian Tironi collection is today in the Museo del Settecento Veneziano in Venice. It is attributed to Pietro Longhi or one of his pupils and dates from 1750. The work is part of a cycle of Venetian scenes created by Pietro Longhi.

The cycle includes other paintings, including "The Visiting Room in the Monastery", "The Making of Embroidery", and "The Stay in the Country". All four paintings are oil on canvas and measure 96 x 131 cm (except "The Making of Embroidery" with 96 x 116 cm). The works are in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Venice Museum of the 18th Century Venetian, Palazzo Rezzonico, is in Venice in the private collection Tironi. The former owner was also based in Venice. The object numbers curator --- 316, curator --- 315, curator --- 317, and curator --- 318 refer to this curator.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson, taken before 1957, has been released. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight discoloration, waviness, and a slight toning. It is torn at the lower right corner, and the top edge has been mounted with Thesafilm.

There is no stamp.

The painting "The Ballroom" is from the collection of the Museo del Settecento Veneziano in Venice and was previously in the private Tironi collection in Venice. It is attributed to the painter Pietro Falca and dates to around 1750. The painting is part of a cycle of Venetian scenes and is oil on canvas measuring 96 x 131 cm. Other works from this cycle are in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. 

The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also houses other works from this cycle of Venetian scenes. These include "The Visitation Room in the Monastery", "The Making of Embroidery", and "The Country Retreat", all oil on canvas measuring 96 x 131 cm, or 96 x 116 cm.

The curator of the Venice Museum of the 18th Century Venetian, Palazzo Rezzonico, is the private Tironi collection of Venice. Previously, the object was in a private collection in Venice. The curator of the object is also associated with the numbers 316, 315, 317, and 318.
A photograph from the raro-art museum dating back to 1940. It is an albumen print, fully adhered. The print is faded and shows two edges glued together. There is a stamp on the back.

The painter Fra Angelico, also known as Beato Angelico, Giovanni da Fiesole, or Giovanni Pieri, created the panel painting "Seated Madonna". The painting is on wood and painted with tempera. The "Seated Madonna" is today in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager is the Florenz Museo di San Marco.
A black and white photograph from 1976 shows the entire BAS NA Camp complex. Access to the photograph is restricted.

The Campanile of the Duomo Assunta in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built between 1701 and 1800. The Madonna delle Grazie is an oil painting on canvas. The work is 11 feet high and 5 feet wide (+3 feet in depth). It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A photograph of Venice held in the Museo del Settecento Veneziano is a rare artwork from before 1957. It is an albumen print that has been fully adhered. Over time, the photograph has faded and shows toning and wave formation. The photograph is wavy and lacks a stamp.

The painting "The Horse Ride" was created by Pietro Longhi around 1755. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 61 x 58 cm. The work is in the Museo del Settecento Veneziano in Venice and was previously in the private Tironi collection in Venice. 

The painter Pietro Falca was also involved in the creation of the painting. The first scholarly mention of the work is found in Pietro Pignatti's publication from 1968.
The administrator of the object is the Venice Museo del Settecento Veneziano, Palazzo Rezzonico 256. Previously, it was in a private collection in Venice, the Tironi Collection.

A museum photograph, considered a rarity, dates from between 1940 and 1944. It is an albumen print and bears the number 254. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight fading. On the reverse side is a stamp with the inscription "Rs."

The "Holy Family" was painted by the artist Sofonisba Anguissola. The painting is an oil on canvas measuring 36.7 x 31.9 cm. It is in the possession of the Accademia Carrara in Bergamo. The work was presented in 1995 by Ferino-Pagden in the catalogue "Sofonisba Anguissola" under catalogue number 48.

The "Holy Family" is documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator is the Bergamo Accademia Carrara 982 (605).

A rare photograph by Alinari Anderson, dated before 1958, is presented as an albumen print. The image is fully mounted and shows slight toning and slight separation at the right edge. The condition of the photograph is described as K: slightly curved and Rs.: Fox. No stamp is present.

The painting "Self-Portrait" is by the Italian painter Sofonisba Anguissola and was created around 1558 in Cremona. The oval painting is oil on canvas and measures 44.8 x 34.2 cm. It is in the possession of the Museo Poldi Pezzoli in Milan.
The administrator of the property is the Mailand Museo Poldi Pezzoli.
A photograph by Alinari Brogi, number 2357, depicts a work of art created after 1953. It is a silver gelatin print.

The Kunsthistorisches Institute in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome, owns three panel paintings by Fra Angelico that are part of a cycle depicting the Passion of Jesus. The works were created between 1451 and 1453 for the "silver chest" of the Santissima Annunziata in Florence. The patron was Piero de' Medici, who commissioned the furnishings for his private chapel. The three paintings are: "Christ Stripped of His Garments", "Flagellation of Christ", and "The Kiss of Judas". All three works are tempera paintings on wood and measure 39 x 39 cm.
The property manager is Florenz Museo di San Marco.

A rare photograph from the Museo di San Marco dating from between 1940 and 1944 was captured on an albumen print. The photograph is fully adhered and shows fading. Two adhesive stamps are present on the back, stuck together. 

Stamps are present.

The curator of the Museo di San Marco in Florence, Fra Angelico, was responsible for the creation of various works of art. Among his most famous works is the door decoration of the "silver chest" for the church of Santissima Annunziata, which was created around 1451/1453. The chest was used to store valuable votive offerings and was commissioned by Piero de' Medici. Angelico also painted the panel paintings "Christ Stripped of His Garments", "The Flagellation of Christ", and "The Kiss of Judas", all painted in tempera on wood and measuring 39 x 39 cm. 

These works are now in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The property manager is the Florenz Museo di San Marco.
A photograph from the museum, part of a rare collection of artworks from 1953 to 1956. It is an Aristotype numbered 251, released and fully adhered. On the back is a stamp with the initials "Rs."

The portrait of Bianca Ponzoni Anguissola was published in 1705 by the administrator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Library of Berlin. The painting, a canvas on panel, depicts Bianca Ponzoni Anguissola and is oil on canvas. It measures 100 x 76.2 cm. The inscription "Sophonisba/Angusola/virgo/F./15.5.7" can be found to the left of the chair's backrest. The work is part of the Gemäldegalerie collection of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Library of Berlin and was illustrated in the complete catalogue in 1996.
The Berlin State Library, part of the Prussian Cultural Heritage, has been managed by a curator since 1705.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00044148.tif, was taken on November 11, 2020. The photograph depicts an artwork numbered 2020.11.11 and titled "Fontolan, Enrico". It was created on October 1, 2020, as part of the photo campaign 30/2020. The image shows the full view of the artwork without a frame. The self-portrait of the painter Laurent Pécheux was created in 1792 in Turin. The oil painting on wood panel depicts the artist in a detailed portrait. The work measures 61.5 x 51.5 cm and is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. Pécheux signed the painting with the year 1792 in the upper right corner. On the back is another signature: "Eques Laurentius Pecheux Lugdunensis Victory Amedeus Sab. regis protopictor se ipsum pinxit Taurini 1792".

The self-portrait was documented in the publication "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret (2008) and in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome (2020.11.11).
The custodian of the object is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, located in Palazzo Barberini, Room 5030. The branch is F.N. and the depot number is D 31.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated bhim00044147.tif, depicts a work of art from 2020. It was photographed on November 11, 2020, and bears the color designation "F". The photograph was taken as part of a photo campaign by Enrico Fontolan in October 2020 (No. 30/2020). The image shows the full view of the artwork with its frame.

Permission for publication was granted on November 11, 2020.

The self-portrait of the painter Laurent Pécheux was created in Turin in 1792. The oil painting on wood measures 61.5 x 51.5 cm. Pécheux signed the work in the upper right corner with "1792 Laur.Pecheux". On the back of the painting is another signature: "1792 Eques Laurentius Pecheux Lugdunensis Victory Amedeus Sab. regis protopictor se ipsum pinxit Taurini 1792". The work is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is located in the Palazzo Barberini. The exact address is 5030 F.N. D 31.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00044149.tif, was taken on November 11, 2020. The photograph is part of the artworks collection and is numbered 2020.11.11. Release for publication was granted on October 1, 2020.

This self-portrait was painted by Laurent Pécheux in 1792 in Turin. The oil painting on wood is 61.5 x 51.5 cm in size. It is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome, Palazzo Barberini. The signature on the front reads "1792 Laur.Pecheux". On the back there is another signature: "1792 Eques Laurentius Pecheux Lugdunensis Victory Amedeus Sab. regis protopictor se ipsum pinxit Taurini 1792".

The artist describes himself as "protopictor" of King Amadeus Sab. and emphasizes his victory over time. The work was mentioned in the publication "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" by Mochi and Voudret (2008) and in the Bibliotheca Hertziana (2020).
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is located in the Palazzo Barberini. The exact address is Palazzo Barberini 5030 F.N. D 31.

A rare silver gelatin print of the famous Vasari portrait from the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome is available. The photograph is unmounted and shows slight signs of wear. The print was inscribed by G. S. Hoogewerff and annotated with his assessment of the attribution.

A painting by the Dutch painter Bartholomeus van der Helst, attributed by G. J. Hoogewerff in 1946 in Rome. It is a portrait of a gentleman, executed as a panel painting on canvas. The painting measures 88 x 64 cm and is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager is unknown.

A digital photograph of the artwork "Sigismondi, Roberto" from 1381.192.tif was created on July 4, 2023. The photograph is designated bhex-2022-35-192 and is part of the collection art 2023.07.04. The Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio houses a painting executed in 1598 by Felice Damiani. The work depicts Christ at the Last Supper, served by angels. The painting is part of the Palazzo Ducale collection, the property of the Comune di Gubbio. The Hertziana Library in Rome has recorded the dimensions of the painting with frame.

The Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio owns the painting "Christus von Engeln am Esstisch". The painting was painted in 1598 by Felice Damiani and is an oil painting on canvas. It depicts Christ being served by angels at the table. The work measures 315 x 190 cm and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is Gubbio Palazzo Ducale. The owner of the building is the municipality of Gubbio, which acquired the property in 1368.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1381.191.tif was acquired on July 4, 2023, as part of order 35/2022. The file is named bhex-2022-35-191 and belongs to the art collection. The view with frame was released. The photograph is in color.

Roberto Sigismondi is the artist of the work. Copyright is shared.

The painting "Mary with Child between the Saints Ubaldo, Sebastian, Catherine of Alexandria, Francis of Assisi and the Donor Francesco Tondi" was painted in 1610 by Virgilio Nucci. The work is an oil painting on canvas measuring 205.5 x 144 cm. It was formerly in the Museo Civico Palazzo dei Consoli Pinacoteca in Gubbio and is now stored in the depot of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio. The owner of the painting is the Comune di Gubbio. 

The painting was formerly managed by the San Bendetto Monastery in Gubbio. The inscription on the painting dates the work to 1610 and names the artist Virgilio Nucci and the donor Francesco Tondi.

The property manager is Gubbio Palazzo Ducale. The owner of the property is Gubbio Comune di Gubbio, which has owned it since 1373. Previously, the manager was Gubbio Museo Civico Palazzo dei Consoli Pinacoteca 6255 Depot.

A painting created around 1835 depicts a portrait of a noblewoman. The work was published by the administrator of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio. The panel painting is unfortunately damaged. A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1381.185.tif was taken in color on July 3, 2023, under the designation bhex-2022-35-185. The photograph shows a full view of the artwork with frame, released for publication. The order dates back to 2022 (35/2022) and the rights are divided.

A painting of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio, Umbria, was created around 1551/1600 by an administrator. It is a damaged portrait of Francesco Maria Della Rovere, executed in oil on panel. The painting measures 61 by 2. The work is part of the ROVERE, Francesco Maria della (1) collection and is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is Gubbio Palazzo Ducale.

A digital photograph from the Museo Amedeo Lia with the number 80-278 has been archived under the designation "bhex-la-spezia-museo-amedeo-lia-80-278". The photograph is in color and was restricted on February 6, 2009.

The painting "Holy Family with the Infant Saint John" was created by Bartolomeo Montagna. It is a panel painting in the oil painting technique on wood. De Marchi, La Spezia 1997, on page 108.

A digital photograph from the Museo Amedeo Lia, catalog number 103-135, is classified as "bhex-la-spezia-museo-amedeo-lia-103-135". The photograph was taken on February 6, 2009, and is in color. Access to the photograph is currently restricted.

The curator of the Museo Civico Amedeo Lia in La Spezia has published the painting "Portrait of a Lady" by Gianbattista Moroni. The painting is an oil painting on canvas measuring 54 x 48 cm.

The research work by F. Zeri and A. De Marchi from 1997 describes the work in the catalogue of paintings of the Museo Civico Amedeo Lia in La Spezia under number 109.

The object is numbered 135.

A heliogravure by Franz Bruckmann from Munich, exhibited at the rar-art fair in Munich in 2011. The work comes from the estate of Hans Werner Schmidt and measures 17.2 x 22 cm. The heliogravure is unframed and has been released.

The curator of the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig has published the painting "Morning Landscape (Aurora)" by Adam Elsheimer. Andrews in his catalogue raisonné "Adam Elsheimer, Catalogue of Paintings, Drawings and Etchings" from 1985, catalogue number 18. A photograph is held in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig is the museum itself.

The painting depicts a portrait of Vittoria Accoramboni and was probably created between 1651 and 1700. It is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 65.5 x 49 cm. The work is part of collection 61 BB 2 of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio and is under the responsibility of the Palazzo Ducale manager. The owner of the Palazzo Ducale is the municipality of Gubbio. The painting "Resting Peasants by a Well" is an oil painting on canvas measuring 49.5 x 38.5 cm. It dates from 1892 and was bequeathed to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome through the Donazione Torlonia. For a long time, the work was attributed to Michelangelo Cerquozzi, but there are also alternative attributions to the painters Sweerts, Michiel, or Johannes Lingelbach. Earlier attributions linked the painter Pieter Jacobsz. van Laer to the painting.

The scholarly literature on the depiction of peasants by a well is addressed in the publication "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret (2008). The work is documented on page 148 and is part of the Palazzo Barberini collection in Rome.

The painter Michelangelo Cerquozzi is credited with the painting "Resting Peasants by a Well". The work, an oil painting on canvas, was created around 1630. It measures 49.5 x 38.5 cm and is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The painting was donated in 1892 by the Torlonia family.

However, there have also been alternative attributions for the painting. Among others, the painters Michiel Sweerts and Johannes Lingelbach were considered as possible authors. Earlier, the work was even attributed to the Dutch painter Pieter Jacobsz. van Laer. Art historians L. Mochi Onori and R. Voudret have examined the painting in the catalog "Galleria nazionale d'arte antica: Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" from 2008.

The painting "Lamentation of Christ (and Apostles at the Open Tomb of Christ)" was created in Naples by Pedro de Rubiales, a Spanish painter. The painting is housed in the Cappella della Sommaria chapel in the Castel Capuano. The oil painting on wood measures 270 x 150 cm and depicts the scene of the Lamentation of Christ with the Apostles at the Open Tomb.

Rubiales was born in Toledo and worked in Rome. He is known for his work on the decoration of the Palace in Naples. The painting is estimated to date from 1548/1552.

The panel painting "Throned Madonna with Child and the Donor Raynaldus" is located in the Museo del Duomo in Anagni. The painting was created in 1325 and commissioned by the priest and cleric Raynaldus. The tempera painting on wood measures 11 F 42 22 11 (+5) centimeters. On the back of the panel there is an inscription that reads: "Hoc op(us) fieri fecit do(mi)n(us) Raynald(us)/ pre(s)biter et cl(eri)c(us) isti(us) eccl(es)ie sub/ an(n)o d(omi)ni MCCCXXV, mense Madii/ Ibi sunt d(e) Reliquiis S(an)c(t)o(rum) Thom(as) Archiepi(scopi)/ Cant(aburiensi) Thom(as) d(e) Aquino /et Petri Epi(scopi) Anagnmi“.

The Madonna and Child are united on the throne, while the donor Raynaldus is depicted kneeling before them. The painting is located in the former sacristy of the Anagni Cathedral, now a museum.

A scan of the photograph "Jemolo, Andrea LA135" was created under the name "bhex-jemolo-la-135". The scan dates from 2012 and is in color. The original photograph was taken by Andrea Jemolo in 2007 and is currently restricted.

The panel painting "Throned Madonna with Child and the Donor Raynaldus" is located in the Museo del Duomo in Anagni. The painting was created in 1325 and is tempera on wood. It measures 11 F 42 22 11 (+5) centimeters. The inscription on the back of the painting dates it to 1325 and names the donor Raynaldus, a priest and cleric of the church at that time. 

The inscription also mentions the relics of saints such as Thomas of Canterbury, Thomas Aquinas, and Peter of Anagni, which are located in the Hertziana Library in Rome.

The painting "Christ and the Samaritan Woman" was created by Annibale Carracci around 1593/1594 for the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan. The oil painting on canvas measures 170 x 225 cm and is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan is managed by the Milan Curator.

The painting "Madonna with Child and Saints" was created in 1602 in Montefalco and is today in the Museo Civico di San Francesco. It was made by Pietro Rancanelli, a painter from Montefalco. The work is an oil painting on canvas, measuring 217 x 146 cm. The inscription "PETRUS/ RANCH /ANELLUS /PINGEBAT/ 1602" is located at the bottom right. The painting was presented in 1990 in the publication "Museo Comunale di San Francesco a Montefalco" by B. Toscano. 

It is also documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The inscription provides information about the artist and the year of creation.

A photograph by Bruckmann, a black and white silver print from 1965, is part of the Kestnermuseum collection in Hanover. The work is numbered 35 and depicts the subject "Sodoma, Lukretia". It was released by F. Bruckmann A.-G. in Munich and produced using the photomechanical process. It was attached with tape at the corners, with the lower right corner coming loose. On the back is a stamp from the KHI and a stamp "Gift Br. Heinrich Bodmer 1924".

The painting "Lucretia" comes from the workshop of the Italian painter Giovanni Antonio Bazzi, known as Sodoma. It was exhibited at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover. The famous legend of Lucretia served as the model for this panel painting. The oil painting on poplar wood is 83.5 x 47.5 cm in size and bears the inventory number 98 C (LUCRETIA). 

The art historical significance of the painting is documented by the work monograph by H. W. Grohn, "Italian Paintings," which was published in Hannover in 1995 and presents the painting in the catalog under number 104. Further important information about the provenance and context of the painting can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Lower Saxony State Museum is based in Hanover. The Lower Saxony State Museum is part of the Lower Saxony State Gallery. The object number of the object is KM 64.

The painting "Saint Leonard as Patron of the Prisoners" was created in the church of San Leonardo in Viterbo and is probably from the workshop of Anton Angelo Bonifazi. It was created between 1651 and 1700 and has been in the possession of the Museo Civico in Viterbo since 1955. Previously, it was housed in the church of Sant'Angelo in Spatha in Viterbo. The oil painting on canvas measures 300 x 180 centimeters and depicts a procession scene.

Simona Rinaldi devoted a consideration to the painting in her publication "The Paintings of the Museo Civico di Viterbo" from 2004 (Cat. 24). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds further documentation on the work.
The curator of the Viterbo Civic Museum has been based in Viterbo since 1955.

The painting "Madonna del Rosario" with the Saints Dominic, Catherine of Siena, Rose of Lima, and Vincent Ferrer is located in the Badia Santissima Trinità church in Petralia Sottana, Sicily. The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. An impressive fresco of the Last Judgment adorns the entire facade. The painting, executed in tempera on plaster, is divided into three registers. The upper register depicts Christ, the apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. The middle register shows the resurrection of the dead on the left and purgatory on the right. The lower register depicts heaven on the left and hell on the right.

The detailed depictions come from the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

Catalogo sistematico, Rome 2008, p. 149, and by M. Gregori, Giacomo Ceruti, Bergamo 1982, p. 437. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds further important information about the artist.
